signals.topic: npm install opencode-ai silently fails with exit code 0 on x86_64 Linux systems without AVX2
signals.summary: When installed via npm on x86_64 Linux systems without AVX2 CPU support, opencode exits silently with code 0. postinstall.mjs selects the wrong binary (avx2 variant instead of baseline), and the wrapper script converts SIGBUS/null status to exit 0, making the app appear to work but producing no output.
signals.review_reason: App completely unusable on affected hardware with no error signal — users have zero indication that the binary is incompatible. This is a main-flow failure (app does not start at all) with a clear root cause in postinstall binary selection and wrapper error handling.

source_issues.title: [linux] opencode silently exits (code 0) on x86_64 CPUs without AVX2 support when installed via npm
source_issues.evidence: postinstall.mjs selects opencode-linux-x64 (avx2) instead of opencode-linux-x64-baseline on non-AVX2 CPUs; wrapper converts SIGBUS/null status to exit code 0 — no output, no error, app completely unusable.

signals.topic: Session retry exponential backoff caps at ~25 days when upstream returns error with HTTP headers but no retry-after header
signals.summary: In src/session/retry.ts, RETRY_MAX_DELAY is set to ~2.1 billion ms (~25 days). When an upstream proxy returns an error with HTTP response headers but no retry-after header, cap() uses this 25-day ceiling, causing retries to appear frozen for ~3 weeks. No maximum attempt count exists, so the session is permanently stuck.
signals.review_reason: Session becomes permanently unusable for weeks — a severe workflow runtime block. Users cannot send messages, cannot cancel gracefully, and must know the Escape-twice workaround. This is a main-flow failure with unambiguous evidence.

source_issues.title: Exponential backoff caps at ~25 days on headers-present retry path
source_issues.evidence: After ~22 failed attempts the backoff hits the 25-day ceiling. Session displays 'retrying in ~3 weeks attempt #45' — effectively permanently frozen with no user action possible except pressing Escape twice as a workaround.

signals.topic: @opencode-ai/sdk versions 1.3.4+ introduce HeadersTimeoutError regression, breaking long-running sessions after ~5 minutes
signals.summary: SDK versions 1.3.4 through 1.3.7 all fail with UND_ERR_HEADERS_TIMEOUT after ~5 minutes of operation. Version 1.3.3 works correctly. The regression affects SDK-based server/client integrations (createOpencodeServer/createOpencodeClient) used in programmatic deployments.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed regression affecting all SDK versions after 1.3.3, breaking long-running SDK-based sessions. Users with programmatic integrations (server/client pattern) experience hard failures after ~5 minutes. Clear before/after version evidence confirms this is a regression, not a new environment issue.

source_issues.title: HeadersTimeoutError after 5 minutes when using @opencode-ai/sdk versions > 1.3.3
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed regression: 1.3.3 works, 1.3.4-1.3.7 all fail with HeadersTimeoutError after ~5 minutes. Reproducible via SDK server/client pattern. Affects programmatic opencode deployments used in CI/CD or as a service.

signals.topic: Kimi K2.5 model fails with 'Extra inputs are not permitted, field: safety_identifier' via OpenCode Go/Zen providers
signals.summary: OpenCode Zen handler always injects safetyIdentifier=IP into request body, ignoring providerProps.safetyIdentifier. When forwarded to Moonshot API (Kimi K2.5 provider), the API rejects the unknown safety_identifier field with a schema validation error, blocking all Kimi K2.5 requests.
signals.review_reason: Kimi K2.5 model is completely unusable via OpenCode Go/Zen providers due to API schema incompatibility. Users who specifically choose this model are blocked with no resolution. Clear root cause identified in Zen handler code — providerProps.safetyIdentifier is ignored.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Kimi K2.5 fails with 'Extra inputs are not permitted, field: safety_identifier' on OpenCode Go/Zen
source_issues.evidence: Kimi K2.5 requests fail with schema validation error from Moonshot API. Zen handler always sets safetyIdentifier=IP regardless of provider capability. Users must use a different provider or model as a workaround.

signals.topic: !yes command spawns an endless background process causing session deadlock and corruption
signals.summary: Accidentally typing !yes spawns a background process typing 'y\n' in an infinite loop, causing session deadlock and making the session unloadable. No guard exists to prevent !yes from creating runaway background processes.
signals.review_reason: A single accidental command permanently corrupts the session state, making it unloadable. This is a critical session-state failure — users lose all conversation context and cannot recover without starting over. The '!yes' pattern is a common shell idiom that users will naturally try.

source_issues.title: local dos with easy !yes command
source_issues.evidence: Single accidental !yes command spawns a background process in an endless loop. opencode becomes frozen, session cannot be loaded anymore. Reproducible with single command.

signals.topic: SDK Skill creation fails with 'Unexpected JsonNode type in array: ARRAY' exception
signals.summary: 用户在调用 SDK 创建 Skill 时，multipart/form-data 序列化逻辑无法处理数组类型字段，抛出 AnthropicInvalidDataException，导致 Skill 创建流程完全阻断。
signals.review_reason: 用户在主流程（创建 Skill）遇到明确的运行时异常，导致核心功能完全不可用。堆栈清晰指向 SDK 序列化层缺陷，非用户使用错误。该 bug 有 5 条评论，表明社区已有讨论和关注，符合用户痛点定义中的'主流程阻断'和'关键功能不可用'。虽然 count=1，但因是单一仓库文件，review_reason 提供充分用户影响证据，保留为 P1。

source_issues.title: Unexpected JsonNode type in array: ARRAY when creating Skill
source_issues.evidence: 用户在创建 Skill 时遭遇 AnthropicInvalidDataException，堆栈显示 HttpRequestBodies.multipartFormData 序列化数组字段时无法处理 ARRAY 类型的 JsonNode，导致 SkillServiceImpl.create 调用链完全失败。测试用例可见，开箱即阻断核心 API 使用。

signals.topic: beta.skills.create API calls intermittently fail with Cloudflare 520/502 errors
signals.summary: Users using client.beta.skills.create() in the Python SDK consistently encounter Cloudflare 520/502 errors, while client.beta.skills.list() succeeds in the same session. The issue affects SDK versions 0.84–0.86.0 and blocks skill creation workflows. A curl-equivalent multipart upload succeeds, indicating an SDK request construction/serialization issue (likely multipart field naming, boundary generation, or header handling) rather than auth or upstream content.
signals.review_reason: Intermittent API failure blocking a core feature (skill creation) in the SDK. User provides strong evidence: equivalent curl request succeeds, skills.list works in the same session. This is not a transient upstream blip — it is a reproducible SDK-level request construction bug affecting skill creation workflows. Impact is non-trivial as beta.skills.create is a key workflow for power users.

source_issues.title: beta.skills.create intermittently fails with Cloudflare 520/502 (anthropic SDK python 0.86.0)
source_issues.evidence: SDK call client.beta.skills.create() consistently fails with Cloudflare 520/502 while client.beta.skills.list() works in the same run. curl equivalent succeeds. Request IDs are often None, making debugging difficult.

signals.topic: Gift subscription redemption fails silently; account stuck on Free plan with no human support path
signals.summary: A user redeemed a Claude Max gift subscription and the redemption page confirmed success, but the account remains on the Free plan after 7+ days. No billing UI controls appear, and all support channels (portal and email AI bot) are unable to escalate to human agents, leaving the user with completely blocked paid access and zero resolution path.
aliases: Max plan entitlement not granted after redemption
subscription billing stuck on free tier
signals.review_reason: Complete loss of paid service access with no resolution path qualifies as a P1 despite count=1. The user paid for Max plan but has been unable to access it for 7+ days. This is a billing entitlement failure (not a code bug), but it is a critical user-impacting problem: service is entirely blocked and the user cannot reach human support to resolve it. The issue also affects the CLI (claude code) as well as claude.ai web UI.

source_issues.title: Gift subscription redeemed but account stuck on Free plan – no human support available
source_issues.evidence: Gift redemption page shows 'already redeemed' but account stays on Free plan after 7+ days. Support portal returns blank page; email bot cannot reach human agents. User has paid Max plan access entirely blocked with no resolution path.

signals.topic: BetaAsyncAbstractMemoryTool docstring contains sync-only code that raises TypeError at instantiation
signals.summary: The docstring example in BetaAsyncAbstractMemoryTool was copy-pasted from the synchronous class without updates. It uses the wrong base class (BetaAbstractMemoryTool instead of BetaAsyncAbstractMemoryTool), sync method definitions instead of async, and a sync Anthropic() client instead of AsyncAnthropic(). Following the example verbatim raises TypeError at instantiation.
aliases: async memory tool docstring wrong base class
signals.review_reason: Docstring error causing TypeError when users follow the documented example is a genuine DX pain point. It wastes developer time and causes confusion. Classified as P2 rather than P1 because the error occurs at instantiation (early detection), it is purely documentation-level, and only affects users who read the docstring and copy the example verbatim — not all SDK users.

source_issues.title: BetaAsyncAbstractMemoryTool docstring contains sync-only example (copy-paste from sync class)
source_issues.evidence: Docstring example in BetaAsyncAbstractMemoryTool uses BetaAbstractMemoryTool as base class, non-async method defs, and sync Anthropic() client — verbatim copy from sync class. Following the example raises TypeError at instantiation. The sync counterpart docstring is correctly written.

signals.topic: agent-sdk skills tool fails to return data while direct skill invocation succeeds
signals.summary: A user reports that calling a skill through the agent-sdk query() function fails to retrieve data, while calling the same skill directly succeeds. Both use the same model. This indicates a behavioral discrepancy in how the agent-sdk routes skill tool calls vs. direct skill invocation, potentially blocking workflows that rely on skills within agent sessions.
aliases: agent-sdk skill tool no data returned
skill invocation differs between agent and direct call
signals.review_reason: The agent-sdk skill tool silently returning no data is a workflow-blocking issue when skills are used within agent sessions. However, confidence is reduced because: (1) the issue was closed without a clear resolution, (2) the evidence is based on user-provided logs without deep investigation, and (3) it may be skill-specific rather than a systemic SDK bug. Kept because the discrepancy between agent-mode and direct invocation is a meaningful UX gap regardless of root cause.

source_issues.title: agent-sdk use skills fail, but I can directly use the skill to return the data.
source_issues.evidence: User calls skill via query() in agent-sdk and gets no data returned, while direct skill invocation with the same model returns data successfully. Closed with 1 comment suggesting investigation.

signals.topic: toolRunner does not propagate container.id, blocking code_execution workflow with client-side tools
signals.summary: toolRunner auto-iterates without forwarding container.id between turns, causing API to reject subsequent requests with 'container_id is required' error. The only workaround (setMessagesParams) causes either type errors or infinite tool-calling loops. There is no working path to use client-side betaTools alongside code_execution_20260120 in streaming toolRunner loops.
aliases: container.id not forwarded across toolRunner iterations
signals.review_reason: This is a complete workflow blocker for a specific but legitimate use case: using client-side betaTools with code_execution_20260120 in streaming toolRunner. Two compounding bugs make every available path fail — the primary bug causes an API-level rejection, and the workaround causes an infinite loop. The 'there is currently no working path' conclusion in the issue is strong user-impact evidence. Count=1 (single repo) but P0 is justified because the feature is fundamentally broken with zero workarounds.

source_issues.title: Bug: `toolRunner` does not propagate `container.id` across iterations, and `setMessagesParams` causes duplicate tool call loops
source_issues.evidence: Bug 1: container.id is required by the API but not forwarded, causing 'container_id is required when there are pending tool uses generated by code execution' error. Bug 2: Both workarounds via setMessagesParams fail — passing an object causes type error 'container: Input should be a valid string', passing a string causes infinite tool-calling loop. No working path exists for this use case.

signals.topic: TypeError: terminated during streaming with large inputs and multiple tool calls (undici/Node.js 22)
signals.summary: Intermittent TypeError: terminated failures occur when streaming requests with large inputs combined with multiple tool calls, causing complete request failure instead of a deterministic or retryable error.
aliases: streaming request aborted on large inputs
undici fetch terminated error large tool calls
signals.review_reason: User-impacting workflow failure: streaming requests fail intermittently with no deterministic error or retry guidance. The error is abrupt (not graceful degradation), occurs in production-like scenarios (large file creation, multi-tool calls), and the only path forward is absence of large inputs or tool calls — which degrades the core value proposition. Confidence is slightly below 1.0 because the root cause chain (undici version + Node.js 22 + large inputs) is multi-factor and not fully isolated.

source_issues.title: TypeError: terminated during streaming requests with large inputs (Anthropic SDK 0.71.2 / undici)
source_issues.evidence: Error originates from undici's Fetch.onAborted: 'Calling the invoke API action failed with this message: Failed to execute 'decode' on 'TextDecoder': parameter 1 is not of type 'ArrayBuffer''. Triggered specifically when creating files >1500 lines or large source analysis prompts with multiple tool calls. Affects Sonnet 4.5/4.6 and Haiku 4.5 with SDK 0.71.2 and undici 7.18.2. Error is abrupt and non-retryable — no documented retry guidance.

signals.topic: Claude Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 regression: only 1 tool call in Batch API instead of parallel calls
signals.summary: 4.6 models produce only 1 tool call in Batch API regardless of tool_choice, max_tokens, or system prompt, while 4.5 models correctly call 39+ tools in parallel. This is a confirmed regression blocking production medical document extraction pipelines.
aliases: 4.6 models parallel tool calling regression batch API
Claude 4.6 batch API only calls 1 tool instead of all tools
signals.review_reason: This is a production-blocking regression with clear before/after evidence: the same request works with Opus 4.5 (39+ parallel tool calls) but fails with Opus 4.6 (1 tool call). The impact is severe in a medical document extraction pipeline where patient records are incomplete. Although count=1, the review_reason provides strong user impact evidence: the feature is explicitly broken, the workaround requires downgrading to a legacy model, and medical data completeness is at stake.

source_issues.title: Claude Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 fail to make parallel tool calls in Batch API
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed regression: Opus 4.5 with 64K tokens calls 39 tools in parallel, Opus 4.6 with 64K tokens calls only 1 tool. Both 'any' and 'auto' tool_choice settings produce the same result on 4.6. disable_parallel_tool_use is NOT set. Tested with identical request structure, document, and tools — only model parameter changes. Production pipeline downgraded to Opus 4.5 as workaround, leaving patients with incomplete medical records.

signals.topic: TextDecoder.decode() failure on Node.js 22 in AWS Lambda runtime
signals.summary: The SDK calls TextDecoder.decode() with a non-ArrayBuffer parameter on Node.js 22, causing an unhandled exception in AWS Lambda. The only workaround is downgrading to Node.js 20.
signals.review_reason: User-impacting: production Lambda functions fail to execute on Node.js 22, forcing a runtime downgrade. However, P2 because: (1) a viable workaround exists (Node.js 20), (2) it is an isolated environment scenario (AWS Lambda), (3) count=1 without corroborating reports. If Node.js 22 adoption accelerates, this will become P1.

source_issues.title: TextDecoder.decode() fails on Node.js 22
source_issues.evidence: Error: 'Failed to execute 'decode' on 'TextDecoder': parameter 1 is not of type 'ArrayBuffer''. Affects SDK 0.71.2 on Node.js 22 in AWS Lambda. Only workaround is downgrading Lambda runtime to Node.js 20.

signals.topic: Skill invocation via agent-sdk query fails silently while direct skill usage works
signals.summary: 用户在通过 agent-sdk query 调用 Skill 时无法正确获取数据，但直接使用 Skill 可以返回数据。两种方式使用相同模型，skill 本身功能正常，但通过 SDK 集成时失败，导致关键功能不可用。
aliases: Skill tool returns no data via SDK
signals.review_reason: 该问题有明确用户影响证据：用户在主流程（通过 SDK 集成 skill）中被阻断，无法完成预期任务，而 skill 本身功能正常说明问题出在 SDK 调用路径上。影响明显（非边缘改进），属于关键功能不可用场景（skill 是 SDK allowed_tools 中的核心工具）。count=1 且为单仓问题，不满足 P0 高频条件，但因影响明确应保留为 P1。Issue #61 标题过于模糊无实质内容，Issue #59 为功能贡献请求，均不符合痛点定义。

source_issues.title: agent-sdk use skills fail, but I can directly use the skill to return the data.
source_issues.evidence: 用户报告通过 SDK query 调用 Skill 时无法获取数据，但直接调用 Skill 可以正常返回数据。同一模型、同一个 skill，两种调用方式结果不同，SDK 集成路径失败。

signals.topic: ExitPlanMode terminates current SDK turn — plan-then-execute blocked in single turn
signals.summary: When using ClaudeSDKClient with bypassPermissions mode, calling ExitPlanMode immediately terminates the current query/turn. No tool calls execute after ExitPlanMode within the same turn. Any workflow that enters plan mode and then exits to execute actions requires a separate follow-up turn, breaking the plan-then-execute pattern.
signals.review_reason: ExitPlanMode terminates the current turn, preventing plan-then-execute workflows from completing in a single turn. Count=3 across three related issues (ExitPlanMode turn termination, updatedInput ignored for AskUserQuestion, bypassPermissions not executing shell hooks). This blocks the core plan-mode automation pattern used by SDK-based orchestrators.

source_issues.title: ExitPlanMode terminates the current SDK turn — no tool execution possible after exiting plan mode
source_issues.evidence: Tool sequence: [EnterPlanMode, Read, AskUserQuestion, ExitPlanMode] — Bash never executes. Expected: Bash should run after ExitPlanMode in the same turn. Affects bypassPermissions mode workflows using plan mode.

source_issues.title: PreToolUse hook updatedInput has no effect on AskUserQuestion tool
source_issues.evidence: PreToolUse hook updatedInput for AskUserQuestion is silently ignored — Claude continues as if no answer was provided. Workaround requires using permissionDecision: deny with answer in reason string.

source_issues.title: bypassPermissions mode does not execute settings.json shell hooks
source_issues.evidence: Shell hooks configured in settings.json never fire in bypassPermissions mode. PreToolUse hook for AskUserQuestion (configured as shell command) never executes. Same hooks work correctly with --dangerously-skip-permissions flag directly.

signals.topic: PostToolUse hook with updatedMCPToolOutput causes renderer JavaScript crash
signals.summary: When a PostToolUse hook returns updatedMCPToolOutput, the Python script crashes with 'H.reduce is not a function' in the JavaScript renderer layer. The Python-side hook executes correctly but the JavaScript renderer cannot process the response, causing tool execution to fail for all tools on the same MCP server.
signals.review_reason: PostToolUse hook returning updatedMCPToolOutput crashes the renderer — tool execution fails entirely and all tools on the MCP server report failure. While count=1, the crash is in the critical tool-execution path and causes complete failure of hook-modified tool results, which is a main-flow blocking defect.

source_issues.title: Title: PostToolUse hook updatedMCPToolOutput causes H.reduce is not a function in renderer despite correct hook output
source_issues.evidence: H.reduce is not a function (H.reduce is undefined). Python hook logs confirm correct execution; crash originates in JavaScript rendering layer. All three MCP tools reported as failed in UI simultaneously.

signals.topic: SDK hangs/deadlocks when string prompts generate many tool calls with hooks enabled
signals.summary: SDK deadlocks after ~50 tool calls with hooks enabled. Root cause: for string prompts, wait_for_result_and_end_input() blocks before receive_messages() starts filling, causing the internal 100-slot anyio channel to fill up and block _read_messages(). This prevents the 'result' message from being read, causing the session to stall indefinitely.
signals.review_reason: SDK session stalls/deadlocks after ~50 tool calls when using hooks — a main-flow blocking defect. Root cause is precisely identified (buffer ordering bug in client.py). Session becomes completely unresponsive; workaround requires patching internal anyio channel buffer size.

source_issues.title: [BUG]: SDK hangs when string prompt generates more than ~50 tool calls with hooks enabled
source_issues.evidence: Root cause fully diagnosed in _internal/client.py:141 — await wait_for_result_and_end_input() before receive_messages() starts causes 100-slot channel to fill and deadlock. Hooked tools denied after CLI timeout. Full reproduction code provided.

signals.topic: Missing content[type='thinking'] blocks in agent-conversation JSONL output
signals.summary: The SDK's agent-conversation JSONL files (v0.1.35+) frequently omit assistant content blocks with type='thinking' even when thinking is enabled or adaptive with high effort/budget_tokens. Reasoning appears in type='text' instead. Missing thinking correlates with less consistent intermediate results in agent runs.
signals.review_reason: Thinking blocks are a core SDK output feature that are missing from agent-conversation JSONL, causing incomplete conversation logs and reduced agent quality. While count=1, this affects a core product capability (conversation logging and debugging) and has been observed to correlate with weaker agent performance in intermediate reasoning.

source_issues.title: Bug: Missing `content[type="thinking"]` in Python Agent SDK agent-conversation JSONL (0.1.35+)
source_issues.evidence: Type: thinking blocks missing in agent conversation logs across v0.1.35+. Thinking content appears in type: text instead. User reports less consistent intermediate results when thinking blocks are absent. Reproduced on v0.1.52.

signals.topic: RuntimeError on query() cancellation — cross-task cancel scope exit
signals.summary: When the parent asyncio task calling query() is cancelled (e.g., user presses Stop), the SDK raises RuntimeError: Attempted to exit cancel scope in a different task than it was entered in. This prevents clean cancellation and propagates an unhandled exception to the caller.
signals.review_reason: Cancellation of a query() call raises an unhandled RuntimeError, making it impossible to cleanly stop SDK sessions. This is a main-flow blocking defect for any workflow that needs to cancel running queries (e.g., user-initiated stop, cleanup, timeout handling).

source_issues.title: RuntimeError: Attempted to exit cancel scope in a different task on query() cancellation
source_issues.evidence: query.close() → self._tg.__aexit__() raises RuntimeError when task is cancelled from a different context. anyio cancel scope detects cross-task exit and raises. Stack trace fully captured.

signals.topic: Subprocess spawn failures cause query() to hang indefinitely or throw ENOENT, with no timeout or fallback
signals.summary: When the Claude CLI subprocess fails to start (executable not found, missing PATH, wiped env), query() either hangs forever (never yields, never throws) or throws a cryptic 'spawn node ENOENT' error. No timeout, no error event, no fallback. Users must wrap with external setTimeout to detect.
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking: any env misconfiguration (wiped PATH, missing executable, nonexistent path) causes query() to hang indefinitely with no error event or timeout. This is worse than an explicit error because users have no way to detect failure from within the SDK — the only workaround is an external setTimeout. Count=2 from same repo (same root cause, two manifestations: explicit ENOENT vs silent hang). P0 despite count=2 because the blocking is total, reproduction is clear, and the hang is a complete workflow stop with no recovery path.

source_issues.title: query() hangs forever when CLI subprocess fails to start (ENOENT / missing env)
source_issues.evidence: Root cause: spawn() fails with ENOENT, pipe is created but child never runs, stdout never produces data, readline loop blocks forever. stderr callback is never called. The process.on('error') sets this.exitError but waitForExit() is never reached. Reproduction in Bun 1.3.11 and Node.js 22.

source_issues.title: SDK subprocess fails with 'spawn node ENOENT' when PATH not explicitly set in env
source_issues.evidence: The env option completely replaces subprocess environment rather than merging. When PATH is not included, subprocess cannot find node executable. Triggers restart loops in production systems.

signals.topic: Empty settingSources array passed as --setting-sources "" breaks all default SDK usage by consuming next CLI flag as its value
signals.summary: When settingSources is not explicitly provided, the SDK passes --setting-sources "" to the CLI, causing the argument parser to consume the next flag (e.g., --permission-mode) as its value, producing an 'Invalid setting source' error on every default query() call.
signals.review_reason: Complete default-usage break: every user who calls query() without explicitly configuring settingSources encounters an immediate CLI argument parsing error. This is a regression that affects 100% of default usage with no indication from the types. The workaround is trivial only in hindsight; without knowing about the bug, a user has no path to success.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Empty settingSources array causes --setting-sources "" to consume next CLI flag
source_issues.evidence: Blocks all default usage: any query() call without explicit settingSources fails with 'Invalid setting source: --permission-mode'. Simplest possible call (query('Say hello')) fails. Workaround requires explicitly setting settingSources: ['user'].

signals.topic: Token usage output_tokens from assistant messages don't sum to result message output_tokens, breaking cost tracking
signals.summary: When using query() with includePartialMessages: false, summing output_tokens from all assistant messages yields a value that differs significantly from the output_tokens in the final result message (e.g., 78 vs 275, a 197-token discrepancy). Only message_delta events with includePartialMessages: true give correct sums.
signals.review_reason: Cost tracking inaccuracy directly leads to billing disputes or overspend: users who rely on token counts from assistant messages (as documented) get values that diverge significantly from actual API billing. The discrepancy is reproducible with a provided script, affects all models, and undermines the cost tracking documentation.

source_issues.title: [BUG] sum of output_tokens from 'assistant' messages returned by query() doesn't equal output_tokens of the 'result' message
source_issues.evidence: Token discrepancy: computed 78 vs result 275 (diff -197) when summing assistant message output_tokens. Input/cache tokens sum correctly. Only message_delta events with includePartialMessages: true produce correct totals. Reproduction script provided in linked gist.

signals.topic: Prompt caching fails when MCP servers are used in session resume, causing full-price API calls
signals.summary: When MCP servers are included in SDK setup, context caching is invalidated on every session resume, forcing users to pay full price for all resumed sessions. Removing MCP servers restores caching. This affects all multi-turn use cases using SDK-driven MCP.
signals.review_reason: Direct cost impact: caching failures mean every session resume with MCP servers pays full price instead of benefiting from ~90% cache discount. For production systems doing frequent session resumes (the primary SDK use case), this represents a significant and recurring cost loss across every resumed conversation.

source_issues.title: Prompt Caching is failing with MCP Servers
source_issues.evidence: Built-in custom SDK MCP server is not serializable, which makes it impossible to store in session state, invalidating cache at every resume query(). Even after switching to HTTP MCPs, caching still fails with MCP servers present. Removing MCP servers from setup restores caching. Users pay full price for all resumed sessions with MCP.

signals.topic: Race condition in ProcessTransport: endInput() allows writes to ended stream causing 'write after end' errors in production
signals.summary: After endInput() ends stdin, async handleControlRequest() calls still arrive (MCP responses, tool approvals) and attempt transport.write(), throwing 'write after end' and 'ProcessTransport is not ready for writing' errors. Single-turn mode is particularly affected.
signals.review_reason: Production reliability impact with high volume (77+ distinct Sentry errors in 2 weeks) on both macOS and Windows. The race condition causes unhandled fatal errors (ERR_STREAM_WRITE_AFTER_END) in Electron applications, directly degrading user experience. handleControlRequest() not being awaited is a clear code-level bug with a reproducible scenario.

source_issues.title: Race condition: endInput() allows writes to ended stream causing 'write after end' errors
source_issues.evidence: 77+ distinct Sentry issues in production over 2 weeks affecting users on macOS and Windows. Stack traces show 'write after end' (fatal ERR_STREAM_WRITE_AFTER_END) and 'ProcessTransport is not ready for writing'. Root cause: endInput() doesn't set ready=false, and handleControlRequest() is not awaited so races with stream end.

signals.topic: False-positive billing/spending-limit error when using anthropic_api_key — blocks action setup with misleading error message
signals.summary: When users configure claude-code-action with a valid anthropic_api_key (that has credits), the action fails with a misleading 'Credit balance is too low' or 'spending limit needs to be increased' error. The real cause is that the action requires a Claude Code subscription or OAuth token, not raw API credits — but this is not communicated to the user. Multiple users across different environments are blocked from using the action due to this auth-type confusion.
aliases: Billing error false positive on valid API key
signals.review_reason: Two separate users (dan Humphreys and cjbuchanan) cannot set up or use the action at all due to misleading billing errors when using anthropic_api_key. Both keys are valid but the action blocks them with false positive billing errors. Main setup flow is completely blocked. P1 rather than P0 because count=2 < 3.

source_issues.title: anthropic_api_key insufficient - misleading 'Credit balance is too low' error when Claude Code subscription required
source_issues.evidence: Action fails instantly with 'Credit balance is too low' (duration_ms: 180, total_cost_usd: 0) despite fresh $30 API key. README implies anthropic_api_key is sufficient; claude_code_oauth_token not clearly documented. User blocked from using the action.

source_issues.title: anthropics/claude-code-action@beta incorrectly reports billing/spending limit error despite working API key
source_issues.evidence: Job fails at initialization level (before any step executes) with 'recent account payments have failed or your spending limit needs to be increased' despite verified valid API key that works in Claude Code CLI. Console shows no billing issues. User unable to use automated code reviews.

signals.topic: Self-hosted runner SDK crash: dangerouslyAllowBrowser error after v1.0.72→v1.0.79 upgrade
signals.summary: After upgrading from v1.0.72 to v1.0.79, the action crashes immediately on all self-hosted runners with an SDK 'dangerouslyAllowBrowser' error. The root cause is that the Anthropic SDK's browser-environment detection was tightened; since the action runs via 'bun run' which exposes browser-like globals (window, navigator), the SDK incorrectly identifies the runtime as a browser and refuses to initialize. Users are forced to pin to v1.0.72 and forgo security/feature updates.
aliases: SDK browser detection crash on self-hosted runners
signals.review_reason: Action completely crashes on self-hosted runners (tested on 3 separate instances) after a routine version upgrade. This is a main-flow regression that forces users off the upgrade path entirely — a significant experience degradation. Not P0 because count=1 < 3 and only one repo, but the per-instance impact is severe (full crash, no workaround except downgrading).

source_issues.title: v1.0.79: SDK crashes with dangerouslyAllowBrowser error on self-hosted runners
source_issues.evidence: Action crashes immediately on ALL tested self-hosted runners (3 separate runners on Ubuntu 24.04, Bun 1.3.6, Node 22). Version comparison confirms v1.0.72+SDK 0.2.76 works, v1.0.79+SDK 0.2.84 crashes. Workaround: pin to v1.0.72, which blocks security updates. Reported by cthorpe-CLASS with detailed version table.

signals.topic: False-positive account bans triggered by GitHub Actions IP usage during intensive PR review loops
signals.summary: When using the Claude Code Action for intensive PR review loops (auto-fix cycles triggered by @claude commands in PR comments), the account protection system incorrectly flags the activity as bot/scripted behavior and permanently bans the account. The activity originates entirely from GitHub's servers/IPs through the official action integration, yet accounts are banned after normal usage. Reporter reproduced on two separate accounts; a third account following the same workflow WITHOUT the action enabled has not been banned.
aliases: Account banned from CI-triggered review loops
False positive ban from GitHub Actions IPs
Account suspension during automated PR review cycles
signals.review_reason: Account bans are the most severe user impact possible — users lose access to their Claude Code subscription entirely. The controlled reproduction (2 banned accounts with action, 1 unbanned without action, same workflow) is strong evidence this is a false positive from the action's CI/IP signature, not policy violations. Not P0 because count=1 < 3.

source_issues.title: [Possible Bug] False-positive bans when using Claude Code Action for intensive PR review loops
source_issues.evidence: User reproduced false-positive ban TWICE on two separate accounts after enabling the action. Third account using identical PR workflow WITHOUT action has not been banned. Root cause: automated review cycles from GitHub Actions IPs (not developer IPs) are misclassified as scripted/bot activity by the protection system. 26 comments indicate significant community impact.

signals.topic: GitHub MCP server Docker container cannot trust GHES internal CA certificates — action non-functional on GitHub Enterprise Server
signals.summary: When claude-code-action is used with GitHub Enterprise Server (GHES) instances that use internal/private CA certificates (self-signed or corporate CA), the GitHub MCP server Docker container fails all API calls with 'tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority'. The Docker container is started without any mechanism to mount the host's CA bundle, and no configuration option exists to override this. This makes the action completely non-functional on all GHES deployments using internal CAs, which is extremely common in corporate environments.
aliases: Internal CA certificate on Enterprise Server
MCP Docker container CA mount missing
signals.review_reason: Action is completely non-functional for an entire deployment category (GHES with internal CAs). While count=1, the impact is a complete block of a major enterprise use case. P1 rather than P0 because count < 3.

source_issues.title: GitHub MCP server fails on GHES with internal CA certificates — no way to configure TLS trust
source_issues.evidence: Action is 'non-functional on GitHub Enterprise Server instances that use internal certificate authorities, which is extremely common in corporate environments.' MCP server Docker container fails every API call. Self-hosted runner host CA bundle already contains the needed certs but cannot be passed to the container. Root cause traced to src/mcp/install-mcp-server.ts with concrete fix provided.

signals.topic: trigger_phrase matching is case-sensitive, silently ignores mobile @claude mentions due to autocorrect capitalization
signals.summary: The trigger_phrase regex is constructed without the 'i' (case-insensitive) flag. When users on mobile (iOS) type '@claude', autocorrect capitalizes it to '@Claude'. The GitHub workflow-level 'contains()' guard is case-insensitive so the workflow fires correctly, but the action's internal trigger check rejects the comment silently — producing 'No trigger was met for @claude, Trigger result: false' with no visible indication of the case mismatch. This causes the action to silently skip legitimate @claude commands from mobile users.
aliases: Case sensitive trigger phrase silent failure
signals.review_reason: A legitimate user command is silently ignored with no error message, causing confusion and a degraded experience. While the main flow isn't blocked (desktop users typing correctly still work), mobile users lose trust when their @claude commands are silently ignored. Concrete fix identified.

source_issues.title: trigger_phrase matching is case-sensitive, should be case-insensitive
source_issues.evidence: Mobile iOS autocorrect capitalizes '@claude' to '@Claude'. Workflow runs (GitHub contains() is case-insensitive), but action silently skips with 'No trigger found'. User sees no error or indication their command was ignored. Concrete regex fix identified (add 'i' flag).

signals.topic: Usage quota dashboard shows available but CLI blocks with 'usage limit reached' — quota metric discrepancy
signals.summary: Claude Code shows user quota as available in both the dashboard (0-15% usage) and the CLI usage tab (0-18%), yet blocks the user with 'You've hit your usage limit'. The CLI metrics are inconsistent with actual blocking behavior, causing users to be unexpectedly prevented from using the service despite visible quota remaining.
aliases: quota shown available but usage blocked
signals.review_reason: User is explicitly blocked from using the service with no workarounds. Metrics discrepancy (dashboard vs CLI both showing available quota) while blocking occurs is a direct cost-loss issue. Users report being unable to work and expect refunds. Two independent reports showing same pattern. Critical for paying subscribers.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Claude Code usage limit error with discrepant quota metrics across dashboard and CLI
source_issues.evidence: Dashboard shows session 15%, weekly 12%; CLI shows session 0%, week 18%, Extra Unlimited. Yet user is blocked with 'You've hit your usage limit'. Same server-side discrepancy as GitHub issue #22439.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Usage limit reached in 10 minutes
source_issues.evidence: Session limit reached after ~20 prompts in 10 minutes. Error: 'You're out of extra usage · resets 3pm'. User states 'This is a caching issue' and expects refund plus compensation for wasted dev time. Regression from prior behavior.

signals.topic: Excessive token consumption — session quota depletes at far higher rate than expected
signals.summary: Users report that session quotas deplete at an abnormally high rate. Simple operations that previously had no measurable impact now consume 10-20% of session quota. Some users report that MAX plan limits appear to have been reset to PRO-level limits, causing rapid quota exhaustion and unexpected billing through Extra Usage.
aliases: MAX limits reset to PRO level
signals.review_reason: Two users independently report session quotas depleting far faster than expected, with simple operations consuming 10-20% that previously had no impact. One user explicitly reports unexpected financial cost through Extra Usage. This constitutes an actual cost loss for paying subscribers. While the 'invalid' label may reflect server-side diagnosis, the user-impact evidence (rapid quota depletion, unexpected charges) is clear and consistent across multiple reports.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Excessive token consumption
source_issues.evidence: User reports MAX limits appear to have been reset to PRO level. Session quota that should be ~1% after normal usage is at ~20%. Simple things that yesterday had no measurable consumption now eat 10% of session quota. User explicitly states money is being consumed through Extra Usage. Regression.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Usage limit reached in 10 minutes
source_issues.evidence: Session limit reached after ~20 prompts in 10 minutes. User states 'caching issue' and expects refund plus compensation for wasted dev time. Regression from prior behavior.

signals.topic: Khmer script output loops on 'org' token — blocks non-Latin text generation
signals.summary: Claude Code degenerates Khmer script (U+1780–U+17FF) into infinite repetition of the token 'org' after 10–15 valid Khmer characters. All output methods (Write, Edit, Bash heredoc, Python Unicode escapes, subagent delegation) fail identically. Short Khmer strings work; the bug triggers on longer content.
signals.review_reason: Core output pipeline corruption for Khmer script. Block-level content generation fails systematically. One confirmed reproduction with clear evidence of output corruption across all output methods. Affects any user working with Southeast Asian languages, blocking internationalization workflows.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Khmer script (km) generation loops on "org" token — systematic failure in Claude Code
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible on v2.1.86, Windows 10 Pro, Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context). All 5 output methods fail identically. Short Khmer strings (5 chars) work fine; bug triggers on longer content. Subagent delegation produces same corruption.

signals.topic: Agent proactively interrupts mid-task to suggest ending session — breaks autonomous workflow
signals.summary: Claude Code agent interrupts active work after ~10–20 minutes to suggest committing and continuing later, before the task is complete. This is a regression from prior behavior where the agent would work continuously until completion. Users must manually prompt to continue, reducing productivity and breaking expected autonomous execution.
signals.review_reason: Directly blocks the primary autonomous coding workflow. User gives a task, agent should complete it autonomously; instead it interrupts mid-task forcing manual continuation. Explicitly described as a regression from prior working behavior. No opt-out mechanism exists, meaning the feature actively disrupts productivity for every extended session.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Claude Code – Agent behavior / session management
source_issues.evidence: Agent works 10-20 minutes then proactively suggests 'We've got a lot done in this session, should we commit now and pick this up later?' before task is complete. User did not ask to stop. Regression from prior continuous-working behavior. No way to opt out of session interruption prompts. Requires babysitting instead of autonomous execution.

signals.topic: /resume list polluted with internal summary-generation zombie sessions — makes resume unusable
signals.summary: When a conversation ends, Claude Code spawns a new session to generate conversation summaries. These zombie sessions are saved as regular conversation files and pollute the /resume list alongside real conversations. Users report 42 zombie sessions vs 57 real ones (42% pollution). Sessions contain embedded full JSON of original conversation, wasting disk space. No way to distinguish zombies in UI except by file size.
aliases: /resume list unusable due to internal sessions
signals.review_reason: /resume is a core feature for resuming past work. Pollution by zombie sessions at 42% makes the feature completely unusable — users cannot identify which conversation to resume. Disk space is also wasted by embedding full conversation JSON in zombie sessions. Confirmed reproducible with screenshots.

source_issues.title: Session list polluted with internal summary-generation sessions
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible: zombie sessions spawned at conversation end with internal summary generation prompts. User reports 42 zombie sessions vs 57 real (42% pollution). All zombies show identical 'Context: This summary will be shown...' text. Zombies contain full JSON of original conversation embedded in prompt, wasting disk. No way to distinguish in UI.

signals.topic: Telegram plugin: dual polling causes ~50% inbound messages to be silently dropped
signals.summary: The plugin system loads .mcp.json from both cache and marketplace directories, spawning two competing bun polling processes for the same bot token. Since Telegram's getUpdates delivers each update to only one consumer at random, ~50% of inbound messages are silently lost.
signals.review_reason: This is a primary workflow blocker: the core use case of receiving Telegram messages is broken, with ~50% of all inbound messages silently lost with no notification to the user. The root cause is well-identified (dual .mcp.json loading) and reproducible.

source_issues.title: Telegram plugin: single session spawns two polling processes (marketplace + cache .mcp.json both loaded)
source_issues.evidence: Two bun server.ts processes both call bot.start() with long polling on the same bot token; Telegram delivers each update to exactly one poller at random, causing ~50% of messages to be silently consumed by the process not connected to the active Claude Code session.

signals.topic: Telegram plugin: orphaned server.ts processes enter infinite 409-retry loop at 100% CPU
signals.summary: When a Claude Code session exits without signaling its Telegram plugin child process, the server.ts becomes orphaned (PPID=1). It immediately hits 409 Conflict and enters an infinite retry loop, pinning one CPU core at 100% with no attempt limit and no orphan detection.
aliases: telegram zombie server process CPU spin
signals.review_reason: Severe resource exhaustion and process management failure: orphaned processes consume 100% CPU indefinitely with no self-termination, accumulating across sessions and requiring manual kill -9. This is a clear host-level impact that actively harms users running the plugin.

source_issues.title: Telegram channel plugin: orphaned server.ts processes spin at 100% CPU in 409-retry loop
source_issues.evidence: Multiple orphaned bun server.ts processes observed at PPID=1 consuming ~100% CPU each (300% total) with up to 103 minutes of accumulated CPU time; processes required kill -9 to terminate as normal SIGTERM was insufficient.

signals.topic: Telegram plugin: inbound messages silently dropped while Claude is actively processing
signals.summary: When a user sends a Telegram message while Claude Code is mid-tool-call, the MCP notification is silently dropped with no queue, buffer, or retry. The message is permanently lost.
signals.review_reason: Primary workflow disruption: messages sent during active Claude processing are permanently lost with no delivery attempt or user notification. This is a recurring race condition that silently breaks conversational continuity.

source_issues.title: Telegram plugin drops inbound messages that arrive while Claude is processing
source_issues.evidence: handleInbound() calls mcp.notification() with only .catch() for error logging; no queue or retry mechanism; every message sent immediately after a bot reply is silently dropped, confirmed by consistent message ID gaps of 1-2 messages.

signals.topic: iMessage self-chat: messages marked is_from_me=1 by iCloud sync are silently dropped, breaking self-chat
signals.summary: In iMessage self-chat, macOS iCloud sync sometimes marks the user's own incoming messages as is_from_me=1 instead of is_from_me=0. The server unconditionally drops all is_from_me=1 messages, causing self-chat to silently fail for iCloud-routed messages.
signals.review_reason: Core self-chat functionality is completely broken for iCloud-synced messages: user's own messages are silently dropped with no response. Concrete chat.db evidence shows multiple dropped messages. This blocks a primary use case of the iMessage plugin.

source_issues.title: iMessage self-chat: is_from_me=1 on incoming messages breaks delivery
source_issues.evidence: server.ts drops all is_from_me=1 messages unconditionally; chat.db evidence shows multiple user messages (e.g. 'i don't know for now...', 'hello', 'great so did you commit it yet?') arrived with is_from_me=1 and were dropped; this is a primary self-chat use case failure.

signals.topic: iMessage: duplicate permission ack (✅) sent when iCloud sync creates duplicate rows before isDuplicate check
signals.summary: In iMessage self-chat, iCloud sync can write the same permission-reply message as two rows with different GUIDs. The permission-reply intercept fires before the isDuplicate check, causing ✅ to be sent twice for a single reply.
signals.review_reason: Reliability issue causing noisy/confusing UX: permission acks are sent twice, creating confusion about whether the permission was actually granted. The root cause is well-identified (isDuplicate check ordering) and reproducible for all permission replies in iCloud-synced self-chat.

source_issues.title: iMessage: permission reply ack sent twice due to iCloud sync duplicates
source_issues.evidence: Permission-reply intercept at server.ts line ~850 returns early before the isDuplicate() check at line ~866; iCloud sync writes same 'yes xxxxxx' text as two rows with different GUIDs; both pass through handleInbound, both match the regex, both call sendText('✅') resulting in 4 total bubbles (2 sent + 2 received) for one reply.

signals.topic: Playwright MCP 课程安装说明缺少关键步骤导致学生遭遇静默失败
signals.summary: 课程中 Playwright MCP 服务器的安装说明仅包含 `claude mcp add` 命令，缺少 `npx playwright install`、`sudo npx playwright install-deps` 和重启 Claude Code 三个必要步骤，导致学生无法正常使用 MCP 工具，属于课程主流程阻断。
aliases: Playwright MCP silent failure due to missing setup steps
signals.review_reason: 这是真实的用户痛点：学生按照课程步骤操作后，Playwright MCP 工具静默不可用，主流程（课程动手实验）被阻断。虽然 count=1 且仅单仓，但 issue 明确描述了阻断场景（静默失败 + 主流程无法推进），review_reason 提供充分证据，应保留为 P1。

source_issues.title: Claude Code in Action: MCP Playwright setup instructions missing critical steps
source_issues.evidence: 课程说明仅包含 `claude mcp add playwright npx @playwright/mcp@latest`，缺少浏览器二进制安装 (`npx playwright install`)、系统依赖安装 (`sudo npx playwright install-deps`) 和 Claude Code 重启步骤。学生遭遇静默失败：MCP 工具在 Claude Code 中完全不可见，主流程教学无法推进。

signals.topic: xlsx skill generates corrupted .xlsx files causing Format Exception on open
signals.summary: User reports that the xlsx skill cannot create new .xlsx files — the write tool writes data directly which produces invalid file format, triggering Format Exception when the file is opened in Excel.
signals.review_reason: Corrupt output file causing Format Exception on open is a clear user-facing functional failure. The skill cannot produce a valid xlsx file, directly blocking the user's intended workflow. count=1 but severity is high due to complete output corruption.

source_issues.title: how use skill xlsx to create new xlsx file?
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly states openclaw can't invoke xlsx skill execution success and the write tool produces a .xlsx file with Format Exception when opened.

signals.topic: docx skill generates documents triggering Microsoft Word repair dialog, eroding trust with collaborators
signals.summary: Documents generated by the docx skill's docx-js pipeline open in Microsoft Word with a mandatory repair dialog. Root causes include malformed footnote separators, missing required document parts (endnotes.xml, webSettings.xml), missing w:space attributes on borders, and missing tblLook elements. Post-repair file is 25% smaller with no content change. Users cannot share documents with non-technical collaborators without eroding trust.
signals.review_reason: Skill output fails to open cleanly in the target application (Microsoft Word), requiring automatic repair. This is a quality/fidelity regression that directly undermines professional document generation use cases and causes trust erosion when sharing documents externally.

source_issues.title: docx skill: footnote separators and table XML patterns trigger Word repair dialog
source_issues.evidence: User performed detailed XML diff analysis showing specific OOXML patterns that trigger Word repair. Documents open with repair dialog that erodes trust with non-technical collaborators. 25% file size reduction after Word's repair with zero content changes.

signals.topic: skill-creator eval workspace directories are read by Claude mid-session during project exploration, causing unnecessary token consumption
signals.summary: When skill-creator creates eval workspaces as siblings to skill directories (e.g. .claude/skills/grounded-plan-workspace/ next to .claude/skills/grounded-plan/), Claude reads those workspace files during natural project exploration — benchmark JSONs, grading outputs, iteration reports — burning tokens on every session. The ignorePatterns workaround prevents the issue but breaks skill-creator's own Glob-based workspace discovery, forcing manual workspace path input every session.
aliases: eval workspace co-location causes token waste
signals.review_reason: Confirmed unnecessary token consumption on every project exploration session when skill-creator is used. The only available workaround (ignorePatterns) creates a secondary breakage by preventing skill-creator from discovering its own workspaces. This is a recurring cost issue affecting every session, not a one-time failure.

source_issues.title: skill-creator: eval workspace read mid-session by Claude when exploring project, burning tokens
source_issues.evidence: Cold-cache measurement confirms cache_creation_input_tokens identical with/without workspace (7,009 tokens), confirming cost is incurred at runtime when Claude explores the project. User provides specific benchmark evidence that workspace files are read during Glob calls and cause token consumption.

signals.topic: run_eval.py completely fails to trigger skills/commands with claude -p mode (0% trigger rate across all eval queries)
signals.summary: The run_eval.py evaluation framework has a 0% skill trigger rate — no query ever invokes the expected Skill or Read tool, including explicit 'run /lucas:memory-layer please'. This makes the entire eval framework non-functional: all should-trigger queries score 0/3 triggers. The root cause appears to be that claude -p mode does not load or present .claude/commands/ files to the model the way interactive Claude Code sessions do.
signals.review_reason: The eval framework's core evaluation mechanism is completely non-functional — zero skill triggers across all test queries. This blocks all data-driven skill quality assessment and eval-driven development workflows. Though count=1 and single-repo, the complete functional failure of the primary use case (skill evaluation) meets the threshold for P1.

source_issues.title: run_eval.py: claude -p never triggers skills/commands (0% trigger rate across all queries)
source_issues.evidence: User ran 144 total queries across 8 different skills with should-trigger cases scoring 0/3 triggers. Even an explicit 'run /lucas:memory-layer please' scored 0/3. Confirmed in claude -p mode on macOS Darwin 25.3.0 with Claude Code v2.1.71.

signals.topic: MCP stdio 工具响应处理在 ARM64 架构上触发 SIGSEGV 崩溃，导致所有 MCP 工具调用必然崩溃
signals.summary: Goose v1.28.0 在处理 stdio MCP 扩展响应时于 ARM64 架构上发生 SIGSEGV (use-after-free)，表现为每条 MCP 工具调用必然触发进程崩溃退出（exit code 139），100% 可复现。crashdump 确认所有 7 次崩溃均为同一可执行文件上的 SEGV_MAPERR，故障地址 0x8080808080808087 为典型 use-after-free 特征。
aliases: use-after-free in MCP response processing arm64
SIGSEGV MCP tool response arm64 architecture
signals.review_reason: SIGSEGV 崩溃是最高级别用户痛点——主流程完全阻断。所有 MCP 工具调用在 ARM64 上均必然崩溃，进程退出 exit code 139，非边缘问题。有完整 crash 分析（strace、coredumpctl）和环境排除记录，置信度极高。

source_issues.title: SIGSEGV (use-after-free) when processing MCP stdio tool response on ARM64
source_issues.evidence: 100% reproducible segfault on every MCP tool invocation on ARM64. coredumpctl shows 7 crashes, all with signal 11 (SIGSEGV) at poisoned address 0x8080808080808087, confirmed use-after-free pattern. Exit code 139. MCP server verified working in isolation; crash occurs after Goose receives tool response.

signals.topic: 工具调用参数解析对大 payload（>15KB）失败，报 EOF 错误，导致任务中断
signals.summary: 当工具调用参数超过约 15KB 时（如 gh issue create 携带长 body，或写入大文件），Goose 报 'EOF while parsing a string' 错误，JSON 解析器在解析工具参数时意外到达文件末尾，表明响应流中的工具参数被截断或缓冲区超限。
aliases: tool call argument parsing EOF large payload
工具参数 JSON 截断
signals.review_reason: 主流程失败：大型工具调用（如 GitHub CLI 创建带长描述的 issue、写大文件）直接中断。EOF 解析错误明确指出 JSON 被截断，用户任务无法完成，与'体验下降'同等的阻断级别。

source_issues.title: bug: Tool call arguments parsing fails with EOF error for large payloads
source_issues.evidence: Error message: 'Could not interpret tool use parameters for id call_36d45d842b654a26900b87e8: EOF while parsing a string at line 1 column 15596'. Error occurs with large tool arguments >15KB. Root cause identified as stream truncation or buffer size limit in tool argument parsing path.

signals.topic: 窗口/终端 resize 后文本不换行，出现单词截断或错位，影响 CLI 和 Desktop UI
signals.summary: Goose 在运行期间若窗口大小改变（CLI 终端 resize 或 Desktop 窗口 resize），已渲染文本不会重新排版到新宽度，导致单词被中截断显示或错位。CLI 可能与 SIGWINCH 信号处理有关，Desktop 可能与 CSS/layout 固定计算宽度有关。
aliases: 终端窗口 resize 文本截断
word wrapping broken after window resize
signals.review_reason: UI 体验下降，有明确复现步骤，影响 CLI 和 Desktop 两侧，但非主流程阻断。归类为 P2。

source_issues.title: bug: text not re-wrapped on window/terminal resize — words become choppy/split (CLI + Desktop)
source_issues.evidence: Affects both CLI and Desktop app. Words are visually split or chopped at the old width boundary after resize. CLI likely has SIGWINCH handler issue; Desktop likely has CSS/layout fixed width issue. Reproducible on macOS (Apple Silicon) and likely Linux.

signals.topic: 用户在中途务执行期间输入的消息被延迟或未确认，需等待当前工具完成后才能被处理
signals.summary: 当 Goose 正在执行长时间工具调用（如 10+ 秒的 shell 命令）时，用户在工具执行期间输入的新消息不会被确认或响应，必须等待当前操作完成。这导致用户误以为消息丢失而重复发送，在 CLI 表现尤为明显。
aliases: user message delayed during tool execution
signals.review_reason: 体验下降明显，消息延迟确认导致用户困惑并重复发送，但不影响任务最终完成，属于 P2 级别。

source_issues.title: bug: user messages sent mid-task are delayed / not picked up until current tool completes
source_issues.evidence: Messages typed during long-running task (10+ seconds) are not acknowledged until current operation completes. Both Desktop app and CLI affected, CLI more severe. Messages pile up before being processed, creating confusing UX where users think messages were lost.

signals.topic: Zhipu 内置 provider 硬编码 base URL 导致 GLM-5.1 (Coding Plan) 用户无法使用，API Key 有效但返回 1220 权限错误
signals.summary: 内置 zhipu provider 硬编码 base URL 为标准 API 端点，但 GLM-5.1 等 Coding Plan 模型仅在 Coding Plan 端点可用（不同的 base URL）。用户即使拥有有效的 GLM Coding Plan 订阅，也无法通过 Goose 使用这些模型，工作流阻断。
aliases: zhipu provider hardcoded URL coding plan
Zhipu provider base URL override blocked
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用：有效订阅用户完全无法使用 GLM-5.1 等 Coding Plan 模型，所有变通方案均告失败，影响明确且阻断主流程。

source_issues.title: Built-in zhipu provider: hardcoded base URL prevents Coding Plan GLM-5.1 access
source_issues.evidence: Error 1220 ('no permission to access glm-5.1') despite active GLM Coding Plan subscription. Same API key works via curl with the correct Coding Plan endpoint. Built-in provider takes precedence over custom provider of same name. Workarounds (custom provider, env vars) all failed.

signals.topic: Windows Docker 环境下文件无法保存到本地（Windows 路径与 Docker 卷挂载冲突）
