aliases: 文件无法保存到本地磁盘
signals.review_reason: 3 条独立 issue 均报告 Windows Docker 环境下文件无法持久化保存到本地磁盘，属于主流程（文件生成与保存）阻断性问题；另有 Sandbox 容器因路径冲突无法启动，同样阻断主流程。用户影响明确：文件生成后丢失，用户无法获取产出物。

source_issues.title: Windows Docker 环境下文件无法保存到本地
source_issues.evidence: 界面显示文件已生成路径为 /mnt/user-data/outputs/xxx.md，但本地磁盘没有文件，容器内 .deer-flow/threads/ 目录为空，文件完全无法保存

source_issues.title: window下docker运行，沙盒限制无法直接修改其他目录下的文件
source_issues.evidence: Sandbox 限制导致无法修改挂载目录以外的文件，且重启后权限失效，无配置化解决方案

source_issues.title: [runtime] 前平台的视频生成功能遇到了Docker容器配置错误，原因是Windows风格的路径格式（如 D:/）与Docker卷挂载语法产生了冲突，导致容器无法启动
source_issues.evidence: Windows 风格路径与 Docker 卷挂载语法冲突，Sandbox 容器无法启动，主流程阻断

signals.topic: MCP Server 注册成功但 Agent 对话时不可见（工具加载链路断裂）
signals.summary: 用户在 Web UI 中成功注册并启用了 MCP Server，但与自定义 Agent 对话时 Agent 报告看不到任何 MCP 工具，日志中无任何 MCP 工具加载记录。
aliases: MCP 工具 Agent 对话时不可用
MCP server not visible to custom agent
signals.review_reason: MCP 工具注册后在 Agent 对话场景下完全不可用，关键扩展功能不可用。日志无加载记录表明 MCP 工具加载链路在 Agent 对话路径上存在断裂，非偶发问题。

source_issues.title: 创建的mcpserver无法被创建的智能体使用，且智能体告知没有相关的MCP工具
source_issues.evidence: 用户成功创建并启用 MCP Server（Prometheus-mcp-server），前端可见且启用，但与自定义 Agent 对话时 Agent 明确报告没有相关 MCP 工具，日志无任何 MCP 工具加载记录，关键功能（自定义工具）完全不可用

signals.topic: 浏览器 blob URL fetch 失败导致文件上传功能不可用
signals.summary: 在 Docker 环境中（Chrome 浏览器），上传附件时报错 blob:http://localhost:2026/xxx ERR_FAILED，文件上传完全失败。
aliases: 文件上传失败 blob fetch 错误
signals.review_reason: 文件上传是主流程中的关键功能，在 Docker 环境下必现失败（所有文件类型均受影响），用户完全无法上传附件，核心交互功能阻断。根因定位于前端 blob URL fetch 受浏览器安全限制或生命周期管理问题。

source_issues.title: File upload fails: blob URL fetch returns ERR_FAILED
source_issues.evidence: 用户尝试上传 .docx/.txt/.jpg 等多种文件类型均失败，报错 'Failed to fetch file xxx.docx: TypeError: Failed to fetch' 和 'Failed to upload files: Error: Failed to prepare 1 attachment(s) for upload'，在 Chrome + Docker 环境中必现，清除缓存和隐私模式均无法解决

signals.topic: LANGSMITH_TRACING 环境变量在 .env 中配置无效，Docker Compose environment 覆盖导致可观测性功能无法启用
signals.summary: 用户在 .env 中设置 LANGSMITH_TRACING=true，但 Docker 容器中该变量始终为 false，导致 LangSmith 链路追踪无法启用。
aliases: LangSmith tracing not enabled despite .env config
signals.review_reason: docker-compose.yaml 中 environment 字段优先级高于 env_file，导致文档声明的功能无法按预期工作。可观测性（LangSmith tracing）是生产调试的关键功能，用户明确配置但功能不生效。根因清晰（Docker Compose 变量优先级冲突），影响所有通过 .env 启用 LangSmith 的用户。

source_issues.title: bug: LANGSMITH_TRACING=true in .env has no effect — Docker environment override always sets false
source_issues.evidence: 用户明确在 .env 设置 LANGSMITH_TRACING=true，进入容器检查 env 显示 LANGSMITH_TRACING=false，文档注释声称可以通过 .env 启用但实际无效，可观测性功能完全不可用

signals.topic: 自定义 Agent 的 assistant_id 未映射到 agent_name，导致 SOUL.md 无法加载，Agent 以无角色定义的裸状态运行
signals.summary: 通过 assistants_compat 接口注册的自定义 Agent（如 finalis），前端可正常搜索选择，但对话时 SOUL.md 未被注入系统提示词，Agent 表现为没有角色定义的裸状态。
aliases: assistant_id 到 agent_name 映射断裂
signals.review_reason: 自定义 Agent 是 DeerFlow 核心功能，用户注册了 Agent 但对话时完全没有角色定义（SOUL.md 未注入），主流程体验严重降级。用户提供了完整的根因分析链路，影响所有通过 assistants_compat 接口注册的自定义 Agent。

source_issues.title: Bug Report: assistant_id 未映射到 agent_name，导致自定义 Agent 的 SOUL.md 无法加载
source_issues.evidence: 用户注册自定义 Agent 'finalis' 后，对话中 Agent 完全没有 SOUL.md 中定义的角色和行为，以裸状态运行。根因：resolve_agent_factory() 忽略 assistant_id，build_run_config() 未注入 agent_name，导致 load_agent_soul(None) 查找错误路径

signals.topic: Plan/Act mode switching leaves write_to_file tool unresponsive in CLI
signals.summary: After switching from Plan to Act mode (via keyboard shortcut or tab), the write_to_file tool becomes unresponsive and fails to create/write files. The UI displays 'Act Mode' but system state remains 'PLAN MODE', blocking the core file modification workflow.
signals.review_reason: This is a primary workflow blocker. The write_to_file tool — a core feature — becomes entirely unusable after Plan/Act mode switching. Two separate reports (CLI) confirm the same root cause: UI state desynchronizes from system state. Issue 10041 is especially compelling as even the AI generating the bug report was itself stuck and unable to complete its own task.

source_issues.title: ACT MODE (Tab)工具不可用问题 / ACT MODE (Tab) Tools Unavailable Issue
source_issues.evidence: UI shows '● Act (Tab)' but environment details still show 'Current Mode: PLAN MODE'. Attempting to use write_to_file results in 'Tool write_to_file is not available in PLAN MODE'. The AI assistant generating this bug was itself stuck in PLAN MODE unable to switch — a direct blocking of the core workflow.

source_issues.title: [Bug] write_to_file tool becomes unresponsive after switching from Plan to Act mode via shortcut
source_issues.evidence: After switching from Plan to Act mode using the keyboard shortcut, write_to_file stops working. Tool confirmed at latest version but becomes completely unresponsive. Restarting Cline CLI temporarily resolves but issue recurs on next mode switch.

signals.topic: VSCode Extension Host becomes unstable in v3.76.0 — crashes, slow shutdown, extension unusable
signals.summary: In version 3.76.0, the Cline VSCode extension causes the Extension Host to crash repeatedly (terminated 3 times in 5 minutes), blocks VSCode window shutdown with 'Stopping Extension Hosts' dialog, and makes the extension completely unusable. Requires laptop restart to recover.
signals.review_reason: Three separate reports all pointing to v3.76.0 causing Extension Host instability: crashes (blocking extension entirely), slow shutdown (blocking VSCode workflow), and complete unusability. This is a clear regression introduced in a specific version affecting the primary VSCode extension product.

source_issues.title: Extension host terminated unexpectedly 3 times within the last 5 minutes
source_issues.evidence: Extension host terminated unexpectedly 3 times in 5 minutes. Cline becomes completely unusable — always restarting and stuck on error. After laptop restart it can recover but continues failing for days.

source_issues.title: Cline VSCode extension makes stopping extension host slow
source_issues.evidence: Since v3.76.0, 'Stopping Extension Hosts' dialog appears on reload/shutdown and takes unreasonable seconds to complete. Blocks basic VSCode workflow.

source_issues.title: When closing the window of VSCode, a prompt box appears indicating that the window closing process takes a long time
source_issues.evidence: VSCode window close is blocked by Cline extension. Dialog appears complaining about slow window closing process, blocking user workflow.

signals.topic: Cline Kanban model configuration fails — LiteLLM HTTP 500 and LM Studio blank model dropdown
signals.summary: Cline Kanban cannot successfully connect to models via LiteLLM (HTTP 500 / NoneType error) and the LM Studio provider shows blank/incorrect model names in the GUI dropdown. Both prevent users from running Kanban tasks with self-hosted or custom providers.
signals.review_reason: Two related issues where Kanban fails to connect to self-hosted/custom models — LiteLLM returns HTTP 500 blocking task creation, and LM Studio dropdown is blank requiring manual config workaround. Both prevent Kanban from functioning with non-default model providers, a key use case.

source_issues.title: Cline Kanban cannot access model name from LiteLLM (but working properly in cline TUI and cline VScode ext)
source_issues.evidence: HTTP 500 from LiteLLM when Cline Kanban tries chat completion. Error: 'NoneType object is not a mapping. Received Model Group=psn/Nusa-Max'. Same model works fine in Cline TUI and VSCode extension, but fails in Kanban — Kanban feature specifically broken.

source_issues.title: GUI configuration shows blank/incorrect models from LM Studio API on Windows 11
source_issues.evidence: LM Studio provider model selection dropdown is blank or shows incorrect suggestions. Task fails with 'Invalid model identifier'. User must manually edit providers.json to set a working model — configuration UX is broken.

signals.topic: Task stuck in 'Thinking...' mode — ls/echo commands cause indefinite hang
signals.summary: Using ls or echo commands causes the Cline task to get stuck in 'Thinking...' state indefinitely. The extension stops responding and the user must close/reopen the connection and restart Cline to recover. This is easily reproducible and blocks the primary workflow.
signals.review_reason: Two reports (including one explicitly marking as easily reproducible) showing ls/echo causes indefinite hang in 'Thinking...' state. Common commands (ls, echo) block the primary workflow and require disruptive workarounds to recover. Significant UX degradation.

source_issues.title: Stuck on Thinking...
source_issues.evidence: Task gets stuck on 'Thinking...' when using ls or echo commands. Extension stops responding. User must close/reopen connection and restart Cline. Issue is easily reproducible.

source_issues.title: Cline wants to execute this command: Skipped, thinking
source_issues.evidence: ls command causes Cline to stay in 'Thinking....' mode for hours. User must close connection, restart connection, reconnect to project folder, and restart Cline each time — highly disruptive workaround for a common operation.

signals.topic: Cline Kanban fails to restore session state after process crash
signals.summary: After a WSL/process crash, Cline Kanban loses all task cards (they end up in trash) and recovery is unreliable — some cards never restore and others show 'in progress' but don't actually progress. Post-crash session state is not durable.
signals.review_reason: Session state corruption after crash is a meaningful data durability issue. Users lose card state and recovery is unreliable. While count=1, the severity is high (loss of in-progress work, unreliable recovery) and directly impacts a key Kanban workflow.

source_issues.title: cline kanban: not restoring sessions after process crash
source_issues.evidence: WSL crashed (likely OOM); upon restart, Kanban cards were all in trash. 'Restore' operation takes very long and some cards never restore. After restart, some cards are 'in progress' but nothing progresses. Significant data loss risk for users with long-running Kanban sessions.

signals.topic: R2 storage mount consistently fails, blocking backup and storage features
signals.summary: Multiple users report that R2 storage fails to mount, causing 'Config sync failed' on backup attempts and 'Failed to mount R2 storage' errors. Root causes include: duplicate bucket entries in passwd file (s3fs), process 'starting' status not being polled correctly, and container startup timing issues.
signals.review_reason: Three independent users report R2 mounting failures that block critical features (backup, config sync). This is a high-frequency, multi-symptom issue with confirmed root causes (s3fs passwd file corruption, process status polling bug, startup timing). Directly impacts the core storage use case of the application.

source_issues.title: cannot mount R2: "Failed to mount R2 bucket: Error: S3FSMountError: S3FS mount failed: s3fs: there are multiple entries for the same bucket(default) in the passwd file."
source_issues.evidence: User reports s3fs mount error with duplicate bucket entries in passwd file. Error persists even after deleting the container. Blocks all R2 storage usage.

source_issues.title: Can't mount R2
source_issues.evidence: User followed setup instructions exactly and still gets 'Config sync failed' when clicking backup. Multiple YouTube comments confirm the same step is blocking other users.

source_issues.title: waitForProcess and isR2Mounted don't account for 'starting' process status
source_issues.evidence: Polling loops check only for 'running' status, missing 'starting'. Caused intermittent 'Failed to mount R2 storage' on Backup Now button. Fix verified by reporter. Directly causes R2 mount failures.

signals.topic: Container fails to start or becomes unavailable, causing all requests to fail with 'container is not running' errors
signals.summary: Container fails to boot before requests are proxied. The sandbox middleware never calls sandbox.start(), so every request fails with 500 errors. Additionally, Durable Object container allocation can fail with 'no container instance can be provided, try again later', leaving the bot completely non-functional.
signals.review_reason: Two separate but related container startup failures: (1) A confirmed code bug where sandbox.start() is never called, causing all requests to fail with 500 errors — this is a main-flow blocking defect. (2) A Durable Object allocation failure leaving the bot completely non-recoverable. Both are critical and directly prevent the application from functioning.

source_issues.title: Container not started before containerFetch: missing sandbox.start() call
source_issues.evidence: Root cause confirmed: sandbox.start() is never called before requests are proxied. Every request fails with 500 error 'The container is not running, consider calling start()'. Affects all users on every request.

source_issues.title: Container doesn't start anymore
source_issues.evidence: User reports bot completely non-functional after a version change. Durable Object returns 'no container instance that can be provided, try again later'. Even reverting the commit did not resolve the issue. Bot remains broken.

signals.topic: Scheduled cron jobs inside the container don't fire when the container is asleep or suspended
signals.summary: OpenClaw's built-in cron scheduler runs inside the container. When SANDBOX_SLEEP_AFTER causes the container to sleep or Cloudchamber suspends it during idle, internal timers (setTimeout/setInterval) don't tick, causing scheduled tasks like daily briefs to be silently skipped.
signals.review_reason: Two independent users report that scheduled cron tasks are silently skipped due to container suspension. This is not a crash but a significant functional failure — users set up scheduled tasks (daily briefs, periodic sync) that simply never execute, wasting their configuration effort and leaving tasks unperformed. Classified as P1 rather than P0 because the main app flow still works when manually triggered.

source_issues.title: Scheduled tasks / cron jobs don't fire in Cloudchamber containers
source_issues.evidence: Gateway runs for hours with zero automatic cron executions. Manual CLI trigger works instantly. Incoming requests wake the container but crons are skipped for the day. Container also loses Moltworker identity after extended inactivity.

source_issues.title: feat: Add scheduled triggers to wake container before cron jobs
source_issues.evidence: Feature request filed by user experiencing the same cron-skipping problem. Root cause: container sleeps during cron time windows, scheduler inside the container cannot fire. Proposes Cloudflare Cron Triggers to wake the container preemptively.

signals.topic: User configuration changes in TUI don't persist to R2 storage and are silently ignored
signals.summary: Users configure settings (e.g. Discord guild IDs) in the OpenClaw TUI's raw config editor and click save, but the changes are not written to R2. The UI simply refreshes with no error message. Users must manually edit R2 directly to persist configuration changes.
signals.review_reason: Two users report that configuration changes are silently ignored by the TUI. This is a UX failure — the save action appears to succeed but changes are not persisted, and no error is shown. Users are forced to use manual R2 file editing as a workaround. Non-blocking but causes significant frustration and wasted effort.

source_issues.title: TUI Raw Config Saves Don't Save to R2
source_issues.evidence: User added Discord config in TUI raw editor, clicked save, and nothing happened. Config did not overwrite R2. Had to manually edit the R2 config file directly.

source_issues.title: Config changes don't persist - dmPolicy keeps reverting to 'pairing'
source_issues.evidence: User reports dmPolicy setting reverts to 'pairing' after changes. Configuration is not persisting across sessions, forcing users to reconfigure repeatedly.

signals.topic: Moltbot gateway crashes immediately after startup, returning HTTP 500 errors on all requests
signals.summary: Gateway starts successfully and port 18789 becomes reachable, but immediately returns HTTP 500 errors on all requests and then crashes. The container then becomes unresponsive. Reproducible on every deployment with specific clawdbot versions.
signals.review_reason: Single but well-documented case of gateway crashing immediately on startup, making the entire application unusable. The reporter has exhausted standard debugging steps (bind mode, env vars, SANDBOX_SLEEP_AFTER) and cannot downgrade. Issue explicitly references two prior related issues (#90, #106), indicating this is a recurring pattern. While count=1, the severity and the pattern of recurrence warrant P1.

source_issues.title: Gateway returns HTTP 500 errors and crashes immediately after startup
source_issues.evidence: Every request returns 500 immediately after gateway starts, then container becomes unresponsive. Port check passes but HTTP requests fail. User tried multiple fixes and cannot downgrade. Related to #90 and #106 which had similar 'stuck at loading' and gateway disconnection patterns. This is a main-flow blocking crash.

signals.topic: Credits purchased but inaccessible — hosted models unavailable, users request refunds
signals.summary: Users who purchased Continue credits cannot use them because all hosted models require API keys. The credits system is non-functional for paid users.
signals.review_reason: 5 distinct users report the same credits-inaccessible issue: purchased credits are completely unusable because all hosted models redirect to API key requirements. This is a direct cost loss for paid users and blocks the primary value proposition of the platform. The issue manifests as 402 errors even with own API keys, and two users explicitly request refunds, indicating a systemic billing/credits system failure.

source_issues.title: You don't have enough credits? seriously
source_issues.evidence: User has $54 credit but system repeatedly asks to buy more. Screenshot attached showing credit balance not recognized.

source_issues.title: Error: Claude Sonnet 4.5 - 402
source_issues.evidence: 402 credits exhausted even when user added their own ANTHROPIC_API_KEY secret.

source_issues.title: Refund request - unable to use credits
source_issues.evidence: User paid $20 for credits but cannot use them. All models require API keys. Credits completely unusable.

source_issues.title: Refund request - unable to use credits
source_issues.evidence: User paid $20 for credits but cannot use them. All models require API keys. Credits completely unusable.

source_issues.title: Error: Claude Sonnet 4.5 - 402
source_issues.evidence: 402 credits exhausted error for Claude Sonnet 4.5 via continue-proxy.

signals.topic: Continue proxy 404/401/400 errors block core functionality
signals.summary: Multiple users receive 404 (missing API key), 401 (invalid API key), and 400 (tool_result mismatch) errors when using continue-proxy, blocking core LLM interactions.
signals.review_reason: 401/404 errors represent authentication/secret management failures in continue-proxy that prevent users from accessing LLMs. While some may be user misconfiguration, the frequency (3 issues) and the specific error patterns suggest systemic issues with how continue-proxy handles API keys and session state. The 400 tool_result mismatch is a code-level bug in how Continue manages multi-turn tool conversations, directly breaking the agent loop.

source_issues.title: Error: Claude 4.5 Opus - 401
source_issues.evidence: 401 authentication error: 'invalid x-api-key' when using Claude 4.5 Opus via anthropic provider. Core functionality blocked.

source_issues.title: Error: GPT-5 - 404
source_issues.evidence: 404 error for GPT-5 via continue-proxy: OPENAI_API_KEY secret not found. User directed to add secret at continue.dev/settings/secrets.

source_issues.title: Error: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M Beta) - 400
source_issues.evidence: 400 BadRequestError: tool_use ids found without tool_result blocks immediately after. Causes conversation to break entirely — the core interactive loop is disrupted.

signals.topic: VS Code IDE crashes or freezes when Continue edits files
signals.summary: Continue extension causes the entire IDE to crash when attempting to edit files, making core functionality unusable.
signals.review_reason: IDE crash on file edit is a complete workflow blocker — editing files is the primary function of an IDE. The crash is reproducible and happens immediately upon triggering edit. Additionally, issue #11966 shows high CPU load as a related precursor symptom on macOS, indicating a systemic resource management issue that can lead to crash. Combined, these represent a main-flow blocking condition.

source_issues.title: IDE Crashes
source_issues.evidence: IDE crashes the moment Continue tries to edit a file. Affects both stock VS Code and Google Antigravity (CachyOS, VS Code 1.113.0). No log available due to crash severity.

source_issues.title: Extension causes high cpu load
source_issues.evidence: Extension v1.2.16 causes high CPU load on macOS Darwin arm64. CPU profile attached. Direct precursor to IDE crash/unresponsiveness.

signals.topic: Local autocomplete (LM Studio / Ollama) silently fails — client disconnects prematurely
signals.summary: Local autocomplete via LM Studio fails because the VS Code extension disconnects before the model finishes streaming, rendering autocomplete non-functional.
signals.review_reason: Local autocomplete is a key differentiator for Continue (open-source, no cloud dependency). When it silently fails with client disconnects, users lose the primary productivity feature without any error message. The AST tracker errors and language worker failures indicate systemic breakage. Additionally, the Ollama runner crash represents a related local model execution failure.

source_issues.title: Local Autocomplete Broken!
source_issues.evidence: LM Studio logs show 'Client disconnected. Stopping generation...' immediately after first token. Autocomplete never completes. Logs show 'Document not found in AST tracker' errors and 'require is not defined' in languageDetectionWebWorker. User explicitly states extension has been broken for nearly a year, referencing issue #5079.

source_issues.title: Error: Llama 3.1 8B - 500
source_issues.evidence: Ollama runner process terminates unexpectedly with 500 error: 'llama runner process has terminated: %!w(<nil>)'. Related local model execution failure.

signals.topic: Terminal tool (run_terminal_command) fails on Windows CMD environment — spawn UNKNOWN
signals.summary: In corporate Windows environments where PowerShell is unavailable and only CMD is allowed, the run_terminal_command tool completely fails with 'spawn UNKNOWN', blocking agent-mode terminal operations.
aliases: Terminal tool fails CMD only environments
signals.review_reason: run_terminal_command is a core agent-mode tool. When it fails in corporate Windows environments (where PowerShell is blocked), the entire agent workflow is blocked — users cannot execute any terminal commands. The 'spawn UNKNOWN' error is a direct, reproducible failure with clear root cause (child_process.spawn incompatibility with CMD-only environments). This blocks a critical workflow path for enterprise users.

source_issues.title: run_terminal_command fails with 'spawn UNKNOWN' on Windows CMD environment
source_issues.evidence: Corporate security policy disables PowerShell. CMD.exe is the only available terminal. run_terminal_command fails with 'spawn UNKNOWN' in agent mode. All other tools work. User correctly identifies likely cause: Continue spawns via child_process.spawn directly instead of using VS Code Terminal API. Reproduction steps provided.

signals.topic: Gemini CLI requests hang/stuck with no response — even simple greetings take 5+ minutes or never return
signals.summary: 用户使用 Gemini CLI 时，发送任何请求（包括简单打招呼）都会卡住，CLI 持续显示 'This is taking a bit longer, we're still on it' 但永远没有响应。核心使用场景完全阻断，影响所有模型（Auto/3.1-pro-preview），覆盖多操作系统（macOS/Linux/Win），涉及付费用户（AI Pro 订阅），用户明确表示已有至少 15 条相似工单未解决。
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：用户无法使用 Gemini CLI 的核心对话功能。count=5，跨越多个操作系统和认证方式，涉及付费用户（AI Pro 订阅），且用户明确指出已有至少 15 条相似工单未解决，有订阅取消意愿。属于高频、高影响的真实用户痛点。

source_issues.title: I cannot talk to ANY model, the request gets stuck forever
source_issues.evidence: User reports being unable to use any model — request stuck forever with no error message, just 'this is taking a bit longer'.

source_issues.title: Gemini CLI is taking a long time to load and respond—even a simple 'hi' takes around 5 minutes
source_issues.evidence: Even a simple 'hi' greeting takes ~5 minutes, blocking the main workflow.

source_issues.title: This is taking a bit longer, we're still on it.
source_issues.evidence: User reports request hanging indefinitely with no response on gemini-3.1-pro-preview.

source_issues.title: Google's Most embarrassing product
source_issues.evidence: Paid user (AI Pro) reports CLI hanging 8+ minutes on a single MD file read, multiple similar tickets unresolved, user is cancelling subscription. Explicitly states: 'Why have I already seen 15 similar tickets, but no one is working on them?'

source_issues.title: This is taking a bit longer, we're still on it.
source_issues.evidence: User with Google AI Pro subscription cannot switch to gemini-3.1-pro-preview, process freezes. User asks: 'Why can't the service simply respond to hi within an hour?'

signals.topic: LocalPythonExecutor security bypass: multiple CVEs demonstrate AST-level sandboxing is not a real security boundary
signals.summary: LocalPythonExecutor has been proven broken by two CVEs (CVE-2025-5120: getattr leakage to restricted modules; CVE-2025-9959: class hierarchy traversal to subprocess.Popen for arbitrary command execution). AST-level sandboxing provides no real OS-level isolation, leaving users without a lightweight self-hosted execution option.
aliases: no lightweight OS-level sandbox for local code execution
signals.review_reason: Two confirmed CVEs against LocalPythonExecutor with documented arbitrary command execution (CVSS 7.6). Two separate feature requests (#2125, #2000) independently identify the same root cause: no lightweight self-hosted OS-level sandbox exists. The impact is confirmed arbitrary code execution on the host system when running untrusted agent code.

source_issues.title: Add lightweight OS-level sandboxing via sandlock (between LocalPythonExecutor and Docker)
source_issues.evidence: CVE-2025-5120 (getattr leakage) and CVE-2025-9959 (CVSS 7.6, class hierarchy traversal to subprocess.Popen) both prove LocalPythonExecutor is not a security boundary. Two CVEs demonstrate that AST-level sandboxing has fundamental escape paths. Users running untrusted code are exposed to arbitrary command execution.

source_issues.title: Add exec-sandbox executor (self-hosted QEMU microVM sandbox)
source_issues.evidence: Users are requesting self-hosted VM-level sandbox options because existing local executors lack real OS-level isolation. E2B, Modal, Blaxel require cloud accounts; Docker has high overhead. Users need a self-hosted option with hardware-level isolation.

signals.topic: ToolSerializer.dumps f-string escape bug produces uninformative error messages during serialization failures
signals.summary: In serialization.py line 429, the f-string `{{e}}` produces a literal `{e}` instead of interpolating the exception variable, causing users to see `Cannot serialize object: {e}` instead of actual error details when pickle serialization fails.
aliases: f-string double brace bug in serialization error messages
signals.review_reason: This is an actual bug with direct user impact: serialization failures produce opaque error messages (`Cannot serialize object: {e}`) that hide the real exception. Users cannot debug serialization failures, making this a workflow-blocking issue. While count=1, the impact is clear from the bug description.

source_issues.title: BUG: f-string escape error in ToolSerializer.dumps causes uninformative error message
source_issues.evidence: When pickle serialization fails, users see `Cannot serialize object: {e}` instead of the actual exception details. The error message is completely opaque and provides no actionable debugging information.

signals.topic: Cannot save or load agent memory/state across sessions
signals.summary: Users cannot persist agent memory (conversation history, working context) after a session ends and restore it when initializing a new agent session. Only `save_agent` exists, not memory persistence.
aliases: save load agent memory feature gap
signals.review_reason: A clear feature gap preventing agent state from persisting across sessions. The user's workflow is blocked — they cannot resume an agent with its prior memory. This is a known missing capability (only `save_agent` exists, not memory-level persistence). While count=1, 6 comments indicate broader community interest and the use case is common for production deployments.

source_issues.title: Save/Load agent memory
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly states: 'I was trying to find a way to save the agent's memory after session is done and load it later when initializing agent again but couldn't find [it].' Only `save_agent` exists, not memory persistence. 6 comments indicate sustained community interest. This blocks long-running agent use cases where context must survive restarts.

signals.topic: Codex model 无法与 autoresearch 配合工作（交互式 agent 会意外停止）
signals.summary: Codex 模型在配合 autoresearch 使用时无法正常工作，因为它会忽略 "never stop" 指令，导致交互式 agent 会意外停止，无法完成自主研究任务。与 Claude 模型不同，Codex 缺乏让 agent 持续运行的能力。
signals.review_reason: Codex 无法配合 autoresearch 的交互式 agent 持续运行，核心工作流受阻。用户明确指出 Codex 忽略 'never stop' 指令导致 agent 意外停止，而 Claude 在同样场景下正常工作。这是模型集成的真实用户体验问题，影响用户使用 Codex 进行自主研究流程。虽然 count=1 不是高频，但 32 条评论证明这是被反复讨论的活跃问题，非边缘情况。

source_issues.title: Codex doesn't seem to work?
source_issues.evidence: Codex ignores instruction to never stop, unlike Claude which works properly. Interactive session can't run autonomously with Codex. 32 comments indicating active user discussion.

signals.topic: FilesystemBackend and LocalShellBackend encoding failures crash agent with unhandled exceptions
signals.summary: When FilesystemBackend.read encounters non-UTF-8 files (e.g., GBK, Windows-1252), it raises uncaught UnicodeDecodeError that propagates up and crashes the agent. Similarly, LocalShellBackend.execute fails on Windows when subprocess output encoding differs from locale default (cp936/GBK), raising UnicodeDecodeError in the reader thread and corrupting output.
signals.review_reason: Two independent issues confirm the same root cause: deepagents does not handle non-default text encodings. #2318 causes agent crashes when reading any non-UTF-8 file, blocking core filesystem operations. #2311 causes shell command failures on Windows. Both are unhandled exceptions that propagate to user-facing errors, directly blocking main workflows.

source_issues.title: `FilesystemBackend.read` raises `UnicodeDecodeError` for non-UTF-8 text files
source_issues.evidence: FilesystemBackend.read opens files with encoding='utf-8' but only catches OSError, not UnicodeDecodeError. Non-UTF-8 files (GBK, Windows-1252) raise unhandled UnicodeDecodeError that crashes the agent with: Agent error: {'error': 'UnicodeDecodeError', 'message': "'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0x87 ..."}

source_issues.title: [BUG] LocalShellBackend.execute can fail on Windows when subprocess output encoding differs from locale default
source_issues.evidence: On Windows with locale default encoding (cp936/GBK), subprocess reader thread raises UnicodeDecodeError when child emits UTF-8 bytes, causing ExecuteResponse to lose output and potentially crash. Error: UnicodeDecodeError: 'gbk' codec can't decode byte 0x9e

signals.topic: CLI model selection not propagated to subagent invocations — subagents use wrong model
signals.summary: When the user switches the model via /model command or -M flag in the CLI, the main agent uses the new model but subagents always use the default model. This is caused by ConfigurableModelMiddleware not being added to subagent middleware stacks, and runtime.config not being forwarded when the task tool invokes subagents.
signals.review_reason: Two related issues (#2316 and #2315) both report that the task tool does not forward runtime configuration to subagents. #2316 specifically shows the model selection is ignored by subagents, causing wrong (and likely more expensive) models to be used. #2315 confirms the same root cause breaks callbacks, metadata, and tracing. This is a clear workflow runtime issue causing wrong behavior silently.

source_issues.title: Model switch not propagated to subagents
source_issues.evidence: ConfigurableModelMiddleware is only added to main agent middleware stack. Subagents do not have it. Additionally, runtime.config containing the model override is never passed to subagent.invoke(). Reproduction: start with -M provider:model, subagent still uses default model.

source_issues.title: Task tool does not forward config to subagent invocations
source_issues.evidence: task tool invokes subagent.invoke() without passing config parameter. This breaks Langfuse/LangSmith tracing (callbacks dropped), metadata propagation, tags, and run naming. Subagent LLM calls appear as orphaned observations with no parent trace context.

signals.topic: CLI subagent project-level configuration not detected — feature documented but broken
signals.summary: Users who follow the official documentation to create custom subagents at the project level find they are not detected by the CLI. The feature appears to be broken despite correct setup per docs.
signals.review_reason: A real user followed the official documentation to configure custom subagents at project level and the feature does not work. This blocks a documented workflow. While count=1, the severity is high: users cannot use custom subagent configurations as documented.

source_issues.title: Configuration of subagents not working properly in CLI
source_issues.evidence: User followed official docs to create subagents at project level with Claude Code folder structure converted per docs, but subagents are not detected. The issue was escalated to discussions. Internal label indicates maintainer triage but the user-facing problem is real and documented.

signals.topic: Summarization offload fails on Windows after first compaction cycle — older messages not recoverable
signals.summary: On Windows, SummarizationMiddleware fails to offload conversation history after the first write because download_files() preserves CRLF while edit() normalizes to LF, causing the exact string match in perform_string_replacement() to fail. Older messages become unrecoverable.
aliases: String not found in file on Windows
signals.review_reason: Full reproduction provided with log evidence showing the summarization offload repeatedly fails on Windows, causing conversation history to become unrecoverable after the first compaction cycle. This is a clear data-loss risk in a core feature (conversation summarization).

source_issues.title: Summarization offload fails on Windows due to CRLF/LF mismatch
source_issues.evidence: Reproduced with full repro code. After first summarization offload succeeds, subsequent offloads fail with 'Error: String not found in file'. Root cause: download_files() preserves CRLF in binary mode but edit() normalizes to LF on Windows, causing the exact string match to fail. Log evidence: 'Offloading conversation history to backend failed during summarization. Older messages will not be recoverable.'

signals.topic: Symlink AGENTS.md causes unhandled OSError(ELOOP) crash in CLI
signals.summary: When AGENTS.md is a symbolic link (a common pattern for sharing with Claude Code), the CLI crashes with unhandled OSError(ELOOP) because FilesystemBackend uses O_NOFOLLOW. The error is not classified in _map_exception_to_standard_error and surfaces as an internal crash.
signals.review_reason: Using AGENTS.md as a symlink (a documented compatibility pattern for Claude Code users) causes the CLI to crash before any agent work can begin. This is a startup crash that blocks the entire CLI workflow for users following a standard project setup pattern.

source_issues.title: OSError when AGENTS.md is a symbolic link
source_issues.evidence: Creating a symlink AGENTS.md -> CLAUDE.md (standard Claude Code compatibility pattern) causes CLI to crash with unhandled OSError: [Errno 40] Too many levels of symbolic links during MemoryMiddleware.before_agent. Workaround requires replacing symlink with a file copy. Tracking issue #2255.

signals.topic: ShellToolMiddleware may kill caller process group when create_process_group=False
signals.summary: When create_process_group=False, the child shares the caller process group, so os.killpg terminates the caller and sibling processes instead of just the child shell. This can kill the user's main process during timeout cleanup, causing main flow failure and potential data loss.
signals.review_reason: CRITICAL: This bug can kill the user's main process when using ShellToolMiddleware with create_process_group=False. The timeout cleanup feature terminates the caller process instead of just the child shell, causing main flow failure and potential data loss.

source_issues.title: ShellToolMiddleware may kill caller process group when create_process_group=False
source_issues.evidence: When create_process_group=False, the child shares the caller process group, so the kill target includes the caller and sibling processes. User demonstrated with a test that os.killpg is called with the caller process group ID, causing the parent process to be terminated.

signals.topic: Agents silently fail structured output when model makes no tool call
signals.summary: When using create_agent with response_format=ToolStrategy, if the model fails to make a tool call altogether, the agent silently returns without structured_response key, disrupting entire workflows without any error.
aliases: no structured_response key in agent output
signals.review_reason: HIGH IMPACT: This causes silent workflow failures where an agent returns without the expected structured_response, silently disrupting entire workflows. The workflow appears to succeed but produces invalid output with no error raised.

source_issues.title: Agents silently fail to deal with structured responses when models forget to make a tool call.
source_issues.evidence: When using create_agent with response_format=ToolStrategy, if the model fails to make a tool call altogether (instead of making a bad call), the agent silently returns without structured_response key. User showed test proving handle_errors=False does not raise exception for missing tool calls.

signals.topic: ChatAnthropicVertex token counter misidentification causes SummarizationMiddleware to never trigger
signals.summary: ChatAnthropicVertex returns _llm_type='anthropic-chat-vertexai' but the token counter check is for exact match 'anthropic-chat', causing it to use wrong char/token ratio. The summarization safety mechanism never triggers even when prompts exceed 200K tokens, leading to API rejections.
aliases: token counter wrong model type for VertexAI
signals.review_reason: CRITICAL: This bug causes automatic summarization to never trigger for Vertex AI Claude users, leading to prompt-too-long errors (200K+ tokens) and API rejection. The safety mechanism is completely disabled, causing failed requests and potential cost loss from oversized prompts.

source_issues.title: `_get_approximate_token_counter` doesn't recognize ChatAnthropicVertex, causing SummarizationMiddleware to never trigger
source_issues.evidence: ChatAnthropicVertex returns _llm_type='anthropic-chat-vertexai' but the check is exact match for 'anthropic-chat'. Uses default 4.0 chars/token instead of 3.3. SummarizationMiddleware trigger threshold (85% of 200K) is never reached but actual prompt is past 200K, causing API rejection with 'prompt is too long' error.

signals.topic: OpenRouter x_title parameter causes TypeError on ChatOpenRouter initialization
signals.summary: Since the last release of langchain-openrouter, initializing ChatOpenRouter() fails with TypeError because app_title defaults to 'langchain' and gets passed as x_title to OpenRouter which no longer accepts it, blocking the entire integration.
signals.review_reason: This bug blocks users from using the OpenRouter integration entirely. The default app_title='langchain' introduced in a recent release causes immediate initialization failure, preventing any use of the integration without manual workaround.

source_issues.title: OpenRouter.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'x_title'
source_issues.evidence: Since the last release of langchain-openrouter, initializing ChatOpenRouter() fails with TypeError because app_title defaults to 'langchain' and gets passed as x_title to OpenRouter which doesn't accept it. Workaround is setting app_title=None explicitly.

signals.topic: ChatOpenAI reasoning mode with MultiServerMCPClient causes BadRequestError
signals.summary: When using ChatOpenAI with reasoning={'effort': 'low'} and MultiServerMCPClient tools, invoking the agent fails with BadRequestError due to incompatible JSON handling. The incompatibility between MCP client and reasoning configuration causes immediate failure.
aliases: BadRequestError with MCP tools and reasoning
signals.review_reason: This bug blocks the main use case of combining reasoning-enabled OpenAI models with MCP tools. The incompatibility causes immediate BadRequestError when the LLM tries to use an MCP tool, making the combined workflow completely unusable.

source_issues.title: ChatOpenai based agent using reasoning and MultiServerMCPClient fails
source_issues.evidence: When using ChatOpenAI with reasoning={'effort': 'low'} and MultiServerMCPClient tools, invoking the agent fails with BadRequestError: 'json: cannot unmarshal array into Go struct field ResponsesFunctionCallOutput.output of type string'. Works if reasoning removed, ChatOllama used, or non-MCP tools used.

signals.topic: merge_configs silently drops recursion_limit when value equals DEFAULT_RECURSION_LIMIT (10000), causing sub-agents to silently get limit 25 instead
signals.summary: When calling Pregel.with_config({'recursion_limit': 10000}), the config is silently discarded because merge_configs treats 10000 as 'not set'. Sub-agents fall back to default limit of 25 instead of 10000, causing GraphRecursionError on multi-step tasks.
aliases: recursion_limit 10000 silently dropped during config merge
sub-agent recursion limit falls back to 25 instead of 10000
signals.review_reason: Silent config corruption: explicit recursion_limit=10000 is silently discarded, causing sub-agents to unexpectedly use limit 25 instead. Results in GraphRecursionError on tasks that should succeed. Affects any multi-step agent pipeline using explicit recursion limits. Both internal and external reports confirm the bug.

source_issues.title: Bug: merge_configs silently drops recursion_limit when it equals DEFAULT_RECURSION_LIMIT (10000)
source_issues.evidence: merge_configs({configurable:{}}, {recursion_limit:10000}) returns config without recursion_limit key. Sub-agents then fall back to default of 25, causing GraphRecursionError on legitimate multi-step tasks. Root cause: != DEFAULT_RECURSION_LIMIT check in merge_configs.

source_issues.title: Update recursion limit magic number and explore changing to a sentinel value
source_issues.evidence: Internal confirmation: LangGraph uses magic number 10000 for recursion limit; when set to 10000 it may be reset to 25 during config merging. Tracks the same underlying bug.

signals.topic: _ExecutionRuntime / _ReadRuntime missing 'previous' field causes AttributeError crash in runtime_to_proto
signals.summary: The internal _ExecutionRuntime and _ReadRuntime classes in langgraph-sdk are missing the 'previous' and 'context' fields required by runtime_to_proto, causing a hard crash (AttributeError) when processing graph state in production.
signals.review_reason: Hard crash with full stack trace in production path (GetGraph via gRPC). AttributeError at a critical serialization boundary. Fully reproducible with minimal code. Directly blocks main execution flow.

source_issues.title: langgraph-sdk _ExecutionRuntime/_ReadRuntime missing `previous` field, crashes runtime_to_proto
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible crash: _ExecutionRuntime object has no attribute 'previous' and _ReadRuntime is missing both 'previous' and 'context'. Triggers AttributeError in production traceback at langgraph_grpc_common/conversion/config.py during GetGraph call.

signals.topic: route_tool_responses UnboundLocalError crash on empty messages list
signals.summary: In create_react_agent, the route_tool_responses closure references loop variable 'm' after the for loop without guarding for empty messages, causing UnboundLocalError when messages list is empty.
signals.review_reason: Hard crash (UnboundLocalError) triggered by a legitimate user scenario (agent with return_direct tool called when messages list is empty). Directly blocks agent execution workflow.

source_issues.title: Bug: route_tool_responses raises UnboundLocalError on empty messages list
source_issues.evidence: Fully reproducible: create_react_agent with return_direct tool crashes with 'UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable m where it is not associated with a value' when messages list is empty at route_tool_responses. Stack trace points to libs/prebuilt/langgraph/prebuilt/chat_agent_executor.py lines 970-983.

signals.topic: _infer_handled_types AttributeError crash on TypeVar and non-class type annotations
signals.summary: _infer_handled_types in tool_node crashes with AttributeError when a handler's first parameter uses TypeVar or non-class type annotation, because it accesses exception_type.__mro__ without verifying the type is a class.
aliases: tool_node AttributeError on generic handler type hints
signals.review_reason: Hard crash (AttributeError) in tool_node's type inference path. Triggered by any non-class type annotation on a handler's first parameter, which is a common pattern in typed Python code. Blocks tool usage.

source_issues.title: Bug: _infer_handled_types raises AttributeError on non-class type annotations
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible: passing a TypeVar-annotated handler to _infer_handled_types crashes with 'AttributeError: TypeVar object has no attribute __mro__'. Also triggered by generic aliases like list[Exception] or unresolved forward references.

signals.topic: add_messages(format='langchain-openai') silently strips message IDs and additional_kwargs during OpenAI format round-trip
signals.summary: When using add_messages with format='langchain-openai', message IDs are silently set to None and custom additional_kwargs (e.g., UI widgets, metadata) are silently dropped. Caused by _format_messages calling convert_to_openai_messages without include_id=True.
aliases: OpenAI format round-trip loses message IDs
signals.review_reason: Silent data loss of message IDs and custom kwargs during a format round-trip. Breaks message deduplication, tracing, and UI widget metadata. No error raised, making it a stealth data integrity issue affecting any OpenAI-format integration.

source_issues.title: bug: add_messages(format="langchain-openai") strips message IDs and additional_kwargs
source_issues.evidence: HumanMessage(id='msg-1') passed through add_messages with format='langchain-openai' returns id=None instead of 'msg-1'. Custom additional_kwargs like {widgets:[{type:carousel}]} are silently dropped to {}. No error raised — silent data loss.

signals.topic: 离线/网络受限环境下插件无法安装，核心功能阻断
signals.summary: 离线或网络受限时，本地插件安装因依赖下载失败而完全无法工作，涉及网络超时(#34242)、离线签名验证(#34263)、Docker部署decode错误(#34274)等多个根因场景。
signals.review_reason: 插件生态是Dify扩展能力核心，4条issue覆盖离线安装失败(阻断)、网络超时(阻断)、Docker部署签名decode错误(阻断)等不同场景，且在版本1.13.x回归(旧版正常)，属于主流程阻断性bug，影响离线/内网企业用户群体。

source_issues.title: Cannot install or upgrade plugin
source_issues.evidence: 插件安装/升级失败，日志显示UV_HTTP_TIMEOUT=30s超时，用户无法安装或升级任何插件（1.13.3版本）。

source_issues.title: Fail to install plugin offline
source_issues.evidence: 从1.12.x升级到1.13.3后离线无法安装/升级插件，plugin_daemon日志显示'record not found'，设置FORCE_VERIFYING_SIGNATURE=false在旧版有效但1.13.3无效。

source_issues.title: Local plugin package installation fails in Docker deployment due to plugin_daemon decode/from_identifier 400
source_issues.evidence: Docker官方部署方式下，上传.difypkg本地插件包成功，但点击安装时API调用plugin_daemon的decode_plugin_from_identifier返回400错误，PluginUniqueIdentifier字段验证失败。

source_issues.title: Packages were unavailable because the network was disabled
source_issues.evidence: 本地插件安装时依赖google-auth==2.41.1无法从网络获取，离线环境下Plugin系统完全失效。

signals.topic: MCP工具/节点在版本升级后不可用或超时
signals.summary: 从1.7.1升级到1.14.0-rc1后HTTP类型MCP工具彻底不可用；MCP节点在1.13.0版本出现504网关超时，导致工作流失败。
signals.review_reason: MCP是Dify工作流工具生态的重要组成部分，2条issue覆盖了升级后功能断裂(需手动DB干预才可临时绕过)和504超时导致工作流失败两种不同根因，均影响核心工作流执行能力。

source_issues.title: I can't use mcp tools when i update Dify to 1.14.0-rc1 from 1.7.1
source_issues.evidence: HTTP类型MCP服务器工具在1.14.0-rc1完全不可用，用户需手动修改数据库workflow feature_info将sandbox从false改为true，或使用runtimeOptionSandboxed而非runtimeOptionClassic才可绕过。

source_issues.title: mcp node failed to perform with 504 gateway timeout
source_issues.evidence: MCP节点(从chatflow转换)在1.13.0版本报504网关超时，工作流完全失败；旧版1.6.0正常工作，同一请求能到达后端。

signals.topic: 知识检索节点性能极差，导致工作流严重延迟
signals.summary: 知识检索节点处理10+数据集/1000+文档时延迟高达1分钟，根因是fetch_model_providers函数调用链中Pydantic序列化成为CPU瓶颈。
signals.review_reason: 知识检索是Dify核心功能，该节点性能问题直接导致工作流执行严重延迟（可达1分钟），影响多数据集场景下用户体验，属于明显体验下降而非边缘问题。

source_issues.title: The knowledge retrieval process node is too slow, causing significant workflow latency.
source_issues.evidence: 用户配置了10+数据集共1000+文档，知识检索节点延迟高达1分钟；py-spy分析确认fetch_model_providers在plugin_daemon通信中消耗大量CPU时间，Pydantic拖慢整个流程。

signals.topic: Cloud端使用Knowledge Base时客户端崩溃阻断工作流和聊天机器人创建
signals.summary: cloud.dify.ai在用户添加或使用知识库时出现TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'icon_type')，导致页面崩溃，所有已存在和新创建的工作流/聊天机器人应用均受影响，无法进行Knowledge相关操作。
signals.review_reason: 虽然count=1，但该问题覆盖整个cloud.dify.ai平台的Knowledge功能，多设备多浏览器可稳定复现，属于P0定义中'关键功能不可用'级别的用户阻断问题，且issue明确指出为服务端bug而非客户端，排除单点偶发。

source_issues.title: Cloud: client-side crash when adding/using Knowledge – TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'icon_type')
source_issues.evidence: cloud.dify.ai在添加/使用Knowledge Base时所有工作流和聊天机器人均崩溃，控制台报TypeError；已在Windows/Ubuntu/iOS多设备多浏览器复现，隐身模式同样触发，明确为服务端问题而非客户端。

signals.topic: Dify Cloud工作流多节点并行执行未生效，节点串行等待
signals.summary: Cloud平台1.10.0版本工作流中多个知识库检索节点应并行执行，但实际表现为部分节点排队等待前序节点完成，8个并行节点无法同时运行。
signals.review_reason: 并行执行是提升工作流效率的核心功能，并行失效直接导致执行时间倍增，虽为单issue但根因明确(并行队列逻辑)、用户场景具体(多节点并行)、影响显著，属于明显体验下降。

source_issues.title: Multi-node parallelism is not working in version 1.10.0
source_issues.evidence: 用户配置了8个并行知识库检索节点，每个包含1-3个数据集，但只有部分节点真正并行执行，其余节点排队等待，导致工作流总执行时间远超预期。

signals.topic: Node.js OSS bundle eagerly imports pg (CJS) causing SyntaxError in ESM environments, blocking pgvector vector store for Node.js users
signals.summary: Since v2.4.2 added pgvector support, the Node.js OSS bundle uses import { Client } from 'pg'. Since pg is CommonJS, ESM environments crash on module load with 'Named export Client not found'. This prevents any Node.js ESM project (package.json type=module or dynamic imports) from using the OSS bundle at all.
aliases: mem0ai OSS pg import crash in ESM mode
signals.review_reason: Two independent user reports confirm that the OSS bundle is completely unusable in any Node.js ESM environment. The module crashes at load time, blocking all subsequent operations. Non-blocking only because it exclusively affects pgvector users (not Qdrant/others), but for affected users the impact is total.

source_issues.title: [Bug] pgvector ESM import fails in Node.js: Named export Client not found (v2.4.2)
source_issues.evidence: Node.js ESM bundle uses import { Client } from 'pg' but pg is CommonJS. Any ESM context (type=module or dynamic import) crashes with SyntaxError on module load. User cannot use OSS bundle in Node.js ESM environments.

source_issues.title: mem0ai OSS: pgvector import breaks under Node ESM (Named export Client not found)
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed same issue: pg CommonJS import crashes in ESM. OpenClaw Mem0 plugin fails for both capture and recall operations with the same Named export error. Second independent user report confirming the same root cause.

signals.topic: Categorization module crashes on import when OPENAI_API_KEY is not set, blocking openmemory-mcp startup
signals.summary: categorization.py eagerly initializes OpenAI() at import time via load_dotenv() + OpenAI(). This causes openmemory-mcp to crash during startup for any user who does not configure OPENAI_API_KEY, even when their deployment uses local LLMs (Ollama, Gemini, etc.). Users cannot use the MCP server at all.
signals.review_reason: Startup crash that completely blocks the openmemory-mcp entry point. Even users intentionally using non-OpenAI providers (local LLM, Gemini, Ollama) cannot start the MCP server. This is a main-flow阻断 issue with clear user impact.

source_issues.title: openmemory-mcp fails at startup without OPENAI_API_KEY because categorization client is created at import time
source_issues.evidence: categorization.py unconditionally runs load_dotenv() and OpenAI() at module import. openmemory-mcp fails during import/startup even when main deployment path uses local LLM, blocking the entire MCP server from starting.

signals.topic: OpenMemory streamable_http endpoint returns 500 error after every request due to missing transport.terminate() method
signals.summary: The MCP server's streamable_http endpoint calls await transport.terminate(), but the current mcp library's StreamableHTTPServerTransport does not expose this method, causing 500 Internal Server Error after each request. Every HTTP MCP interaction fails after the first request.
signals.review_reason: Every HTTP MCP request in OpenMemory results in a 500 error after the first request is handled. This is a complete functional breakdown of the HTTP transport path, a primary deployment mode. User evidence is clear and specific.

source_issues.title: openmemory streamable_http endpoint crashes with current MCP Python transport due to missing terminate()
source_issues.evidence: The streamable_http endpoint calls await transport.terminate() which does not exist in the current mcp library implementation. After handling a request, every subsequent request to the HTTP MCP endpoint fails with 500 Internal Server Error.

signals.topic: vLLM provider silently drops response_format parameter, causing JSON parsing failures during memory extraction and update
signals.summary: The vLLM LLM provider accepts response_format in generate_response() but never forwards it to the underlying OpenAI-compatible client. This means mem0 assumes JSON-constrained output while the vLLM backend only receives plain text guidance, leading to invalid JSON and downstream parsing failures during memory add/update operations.
aliases: memory extraction JSON parse error with vLLM
signals.review_reason: Non-blocking for OpenAI users but a clear silent failure for vLLM users: memory add/update operations silently produce invalid JSON and parsing fails. This is a functional defect that corrupts the core memory storage workflow for affected users, warranting P2.

source_issues.title: vllm provider drops response_format in generate_response, causing JSON parsing failures in memory extraction/update
source_issues.evidence: vLLM provider's generate_response accepts response_format but does not pass it to the OpenAI-compatible client. Result: model returns unconstrained text instead of JSON. Downstream JSON parsing fails during memory extraction and update. User is actively using vLLM and hitting the failure.

signals.topic: OSS Supabase vector store get() throws PGRST116 exception on missing rows instead of returning null, blocking add/update flow
signals.summary: SupabaseDB.get(vectorId) uses .single() for row lookups that may legitimately return zero rows. On Supabase/PostgREST, missing rows throw PGRST116 (cannot coerce to single object) instead of returning null. This derails the add/update flow when checking for existing vectors.
aliases: Supabase vector store missing row exception
OSS SupabaseDB.get crash on new vector
signals.review_reason: Directly blocks the core add/update workflow for Supabase vector store users. A legitimate missing row (new vector) throws an exception instead of returning null, preventing the vector from being stored. This is a main-path functional break.

source_issues.title: OSS Supabase vector store: get(vectorId) uses .single() and throws PGRST116 on missing rows

signals.topic: Python MCP client infinite reconnect loop when MCP server does not implement ping method

MCP client stuck reconnecting without ping support

Clear reproduction with Snowflake managed MCP server, full stack trace, and actionable root cause (missing ping capability check).

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: MCP client connection goes into infinite loop if MCP server does not support ping method
source_issues.evidence: connect=>load_tools=>_ensure_connected=>ping fails=>connect infinite loop. Snowflake MCP server returns UnsupportedMethod error for ping. Every MCP server that omits ping is unusable.

signals.review_reason: Clear user impact in production multi-user scenario: a single MCP timeout kills all concurrent requests sharing the same tool instance. Multiple anyio.CancelledError stack traces confirm cascading cancellation. Affects Foundry Hosted Agent serving real users.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: MCPStreamableHTTPTool does not handle Concurrent Requests
source_issues.evidence: 5 parallel requests sent to Foundry Hosted Agent using shared MCP tool instance; one MCP endpoint timeout killed all 4 other in-flight requests, only 1 of 5 returned 200 OK. Shared MCP tool instance used by multiple concurrent sessions.

signals.topic: Python sub-agent tool approval response does not resume tool execution
signals.summary: When a sub-agent is used via .as_tool() and its inner tool requires always_require approval, the approval correctly propagates to the caller, but after sending the approval response the inner tool is never executed and the outer agent returns without calling the tool.
signals.review_reason: Core multi-agent orchestration workflow is broken: sub-agent tool approval flow silently fails to execute the tool after approval. Reproduced in both streaming and non-streaming mode, confirmed with and without approval. Breaks the primary use case of agent delegation with human-in-the-loop approval.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: Cannot approve tool usage from sub-agents
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction shows user_input_requests correctly triggered, approval response sent, but final response omits tool result. With approval_mode=never_require same code path produces correct tool result, proving the approval response is not properly wired to resume inner tool execution.

signals.topic: .NET Workflow agent does not preserve session chat history across calls

.NET Workflow agent session history lost between turns

source_issues.title: .NET: [Bug]: Unable to get Session chat history in work flow agent
source_issues.evidence: User reports that after converting workflow to AIAgent and passing session, only the last message is available; ChatHistoryProvider cannot be added, forcing manual message list management on every call.

signals.topic: .NET ChatClientAgent throws when using ChatHistoryProvider with Azure OpenAI Responses API in stateless mode

source_issues.title: .NET: [Bug]: ChatClientAgent throws when using ChatHistoryProvider with Azure OpenAI Responses API and store=false

signals.topic: SelectorGroupChat livelock — fallback returns excluded previous speaker when LLM selector fails
signals.summary: When allow_repeated_speaker=False, SelectorGroupChat's fallback logic returns self._previous_speaker — the exact agent that was supposed to be excluded — causing a deterministic infinite loop that blocks multi-agent conversations entirely.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed bug causing deterministic infinite loop in SelectorGroupChat. The fallback path is a direct code defect: returning self._previous_speaker when allow_repeated_speaker=False is the opposite of the intended behavior. This blocks the core multi-agent conversation workflow completely. Reproducible with provided code sample. P0 despite count=1 because the impact is a complete workflow block (infinite loop) with no recovery path within the framework.

source_issues.title: [Bug] SelectorGroupChat livelock: fallback returns excluded previous speaker when allow_repeated_speaker=False
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed bug with reproduction code. When LLM-based selector exhausts max_selector_attempts and cannot pick a valid non-previous speaker, the fallback in _selector_group_chat.py returns self._previous_speaker directly, triggering: Agent A speaks → selector fails → fallback returns A → A speaks again → infinite loop. Full reproduction code provided.

signals.topic: Auto-generated tool ID exceeds OpenAI API 40-character limit causing BadRequestError
signals.summary: AutoGen's auto-generated UUID-based tool IDs are 41 characters, exceeding OpenAI's 40-character limit, causing openai.BadRequestError: Error code: 400 and blocking the core tool-use workflow.

Auto-generated UUID-based tool IDs exceed the OpenAI API's 40-character limit by 1 character, producing openai.BadRequestError (HTTP 400). The error occurs in _single_threaded_agent_runtime._on_message during message processing, blocking the core tool-use workflow. Closed issue with 'awaiting-op-response' label indicates the team acknowledged it. P1 (not P0) because the block is on a specific tool-id generation path rather than a universal multi-agent workflow block.

source_issues.title: Tool id string too long
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed bug with full stack trace. Tool ID is 41 characters (contains full UUID: '5694c56d-6c52-4f8b-8da4-7e5b331e2210/5694c56d-6c52-4f8b-8da4-7e5b331e2210') but OpenAI API max is 40. signals.topic: Trace viewer fails to open large traces (>10MB) due to Service Worker blob limitations
signals.summary: The Playwright trace viewer (both `show-trace` CLI and trace.playwright.dev) throws `TypeError: Failed to fetch` and crashes when opening traces containing large uncompressed `.trace`/`.network` files (typically >10MB from complex/long-running tests). Three underlying bugs in `ZipTraceLoaderBackend` cause cascading failures: `Response.blob()` from a ReadableStream fails in Service Worker context on large data, `DecompressionStream` rejects with `undefined` causing `TypeError: Cannot set properties of undefined`, and the `finally` block tries to close an already-errored WritableStream.
aliases: large trace zip fails to open
trace viewer cannot load big traces
signals.review_reason: Two independent issues both describe trace viewer failures. Issue 39845 is a critical debugger breakage: users running complex E2E tests produce traces >10MB, and the trace viewer is the primary debugging tool — when it fails, the entire Playwright debugging story breaks down. Process hangs and test infrastructure problems compound this. The impact is severe even at count=2 because trace viewer failure means developers lose the only way to understand test failures.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Trace viewer fails to open trace: Could not load trace from
source_issues.evidence: Trace viewer throws TypeError: Failed to fetch and TypeError: Cannot close a ERRORED writable stream when opening large traces (>10MB). Root cause in ZipTraceLoaderBackend: Response.blob() from ReadableStream fails in Service Worker for large data, DecompressionStream rejects with undefined causing crash in zip.js finally block.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Traceviewer - network requests that are 'Canceled' display blank status in trace
source_issues.evidence: Trace viewer shows no status for canceled network requests. HAR file correctly records status as -1, but trace viewer UI displays blank. DevTools correctly shows status as 'cancelled', indicating trace recording/replay does not capture this state.

signals.topic: ffmpeg child process orphaned when no video frames are recorded, causing Node process to hang indefinitely
signals.summary: When video recording starts but no frames are captured (e.g., no browser rendering occurs), the ffmpeg child process is not properly terminated. The Node.js parent process hangs waiting for the ffmpeg stdin that never receives input. This affects both the `playwright` library and CI pipelines where tests that don't render frames leave hanging processes.
aliases: ffmpeg process hangs after video stop
video recording no frames blocks exit
signals.review_reason: A Node process hang with no exit signal is a complete test execution block. Users must kill processes manually. Explicitly reported as blocking production CI (cloudflare/telescope). Clear reproduction steps and the fix exists in main, confirming this is a real bug. Despite count=1, the severity (indefinite hang) and production impact justify P0.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: ffmpeg orphaned if no frames are recorded
source_issues.evidence: Node.js process hangs indefinitely after `video.stop()` when no frames were recorded. `node reproduce.js` never exits. Reproduced consistently on v1.58.2. Reproducer script provided at github.com/sufian-cf/playwright-ffmpeg-bug-repro. Reports being hit in production at cloudflare/telescope. Fixed in main branch 1.59.0-alpha but users on 1.58.2 are blocked.

signals.topic: playwright install fails in sandboxed/restricted network environments where DNS resolution is only available through a proxy
signals.summary: Browser installation (`playwright install`) fails with `EAI_AGAIN` DNS errors in sandboxed environments (e.g., Claude Code remote sandbox, CI containers with egress proxies). Even when HTTPS_PROXY is set, Node.js resolves the proxy hostname locally before connecting, creating a circular dependency. The workaround requires manual browser download via curl.
signals.review_reason: Playwright install failure means the entire tool cannot be used — a complete setup blocker. While count=1, the issue affects a growing class of restricted network environments (cloud IDEs, sandboxed CI, enterprise containers). The root cause is well-analyzed and the only workaround (manual curl) is non-trivial for average users.

source_issues.title: playwright install fails in sandboxed environments where DNS requires proxy resolution
source_issues.evidence: Browser download fails 5 times with 'getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN storage.googleapis.com' despite correct HTTPS_PROXY. Root cause: Node.js https.request() resolves proxy hostname locally before establishing CONNECT tunnel. Full root cause analysis provided with child_process.fork() trace. Only workaround is manual curl download.

signals.topic: electron.launch() fails on Electron 40.2.1 with 'bad option: --remote-debugging-port=0'
signals.summary: The Electron launcher passes `--remote-debugging-port=0` as a CLI argument, which Electron 40.2.1 rejects with 'bad option' before application code runs. A previous fix (#39012) was reverted due to regressions with Electron 39 and VS Code, leaving the issue unresolved for Electron 40.x users of the standard npm electron package.
signals.review_reason: electron.launch() being broken for the latest Electron version means end-to-end testing of Electron apps is entirely blocked. Downstream projects cannot maintain local Playwright patches indefinitely. The fix was previously attempted and reverted, indicating this is a regression risk — but the current broken state for Electron 40 is a clear user-impacting pain point.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: electron.launch() still fails on Electron 40.2.1 after revert of #39012
source_issues.evidence: electron.launch() fails before app code executes with 'bad option: --remote-debugging-port=0' on Electron 40.2.1. Previous fix #39012 was reverted in #39710 due to VS Code regressions. Users of current npm electron package are blocked with no upstream resolution.

signals.topic: video-start/video-stop produces 0-byte .webm files when multiple page navigations occur during recording
signals.summary: Calling `video-start`, then performing multiple page navigations, then `video-stop` produces a 0-byte .webm file 100% of the time (5/5 tested). The screencast stops emitting CDP frames after navigations, and video-stop writes only a white fallback frame, resulting in an empty file. Single navigation works; adding sleep before stop does not help. Also affects headed and headless modes, and progressive degradation occurs even on static pages with repeated cycles.
signals.review_reason: Video recording producing empty files after common user behavior (multiple navigations) is a significant regression. This directly impacts CI/CD pipelines where video artifacts are used for debugging or compliance. The 100% reproducibility rate and the absence of a working workaround make this a high-impact pain point despite being a single issue.

source_issues.title: video-start/video-stop produces 0-byte files when navigations occur during recording
source_issues.evidence: 100% reproducible (5/5 independent tests). video-start → multiple navigations → video-stop produces 0-byte output.webm. Single navigation works. Workaround: close/reopen browser resets the issue. Root cause: Page.screencastFrame CDP events stop after navigations; screencast does not re-issue startScreencast command. DevTools correctly shows 'cancelled' status for requests, indicating trace recording stops.

signals.topic: Azure Monitor telemetry instrumentor blocks AgentGroupChat execution with dict response format error
signals.summary: When Azure Monitor (configure_azure_monitor) is enabled, AzureAIAgent inside AgentGroupChat fails with 'ValueError: Unknown response format <class dict>' because the OpenTelemetry instrumentor does not support dict-typed response_format, blocking all multi-agent execution flows.
signals.review_reason: This is P0 because it completely blocks a primary multi-agent workflow (AgentGroupChat) whenever Azure Monitor telemetry is enabled. The error is deterministic and non-recoverable — all retries fail, and no workaround exists. Evidence is explicit: 'all agent executions fail' and 'automatic retries occur but all fail with the same error'.

source_issues.title: Bug: [Python] AgentGroupChat fails with "Unknown response format <class 'dict'>" when Azure Monitor is enabled
source_issues.evidence: All agent executions fail with ValueError when Azure Monitor is enabled. Automatic retries all fail. Multi-agent flow is completely blocked.

signals.topic: TextChunker overcounts paragraph size by using word count instead of token count, causing silent chunk overflow and data loss
signals.summary: TextChunker.SplitPlainTextParagraphs uses word count instead of token count in orphan chunk gluing logic, causing the last chunk to exceed target length. This leads to silent loss of information when generating embeddings or using a reranker.
aliases: TextChunker token count vs word count mismatch
signals.review_reason: This is a genuine data quality bug affecting RAG pipelines. The chunk overflow is described as 'frequently silent', meaning users may not detect the data loss at all. Embeddings and rerankers receiving oversized chunks will produce degraded retrieval quality. However count=1 and single-repository, so P1 not P0.

source_issues.title: Bug: the TextChunker.SplitPlainTextParagraphs sometimes overcount the chunk sizes
source_issues.evidence: Chunk gluing logic uses number of words instead of tokens, leading to last chunk exceeding target length, causing silent data loss during embedding generation.

signals.topic: Google AI connector leaks model thinking/reasoning text into application-visible ChatMessageContent

signals.review_reason: This corrupts application-level output — users receive model internal reasoning as the response. While it does not crash, the application receives wrong output. The fix for the same issue on function call parts (PR #13609) was already applied, but the same gap existed for text parts. P1 due to count=1 and non-blocking nature.

source_issues.title: Python: Bug: Google AI connector leaks thinking/thought text parts into ChatMessageContent
source_issues.evidence: Model's internal reasoning text (e.g. '**Processing the Task Request** Okay...') appears in ChatMessageContent instead of actual response. The application receives internal thought output as if it were the real answer.

source_issues.title: Python: Getting started jupyter notebook "Building Semantic with Embeddings" doesn't work out of the box
source_issues.evidence: BadRequestError when running the getting-started notebook with default embedding model: 'This model does not support specifying dimensions.' No guidance provided on which model to use.

signals.topic: Chat history summarizer not working — full chat history passed to LLM instead of summarized, causing token waste

aliases: full chat history passed to LLM API call
signals.review_reason: This defeats the purpose of the summarizer feature entirely. Users who configure summarization to reduce token costs still get full history sent, leading to predictable cost overruns especially in multi-agent GroupChat scenarios. The user's own description confirms the feature is 'not working'. P1 due to cost impact and feature unavailability.

source_issues.title: Python: Bug: Complete chat history is getting passed to LLM - chat history summarizer is not working
source_issues.evidence: User observes in debug logs that full chat history is sent to LLM despite ChatHistorySummarizationReducer being configured with auto_reduce=True and target_count=3.

signals.topic: Engine crash leaves orphaned threads causing persistent crash/resume loop requiring manual database deletion to recover
signals.summary: When the Codex engine crashes on Windows (MCP failure, personality errors, OOM, etc.), the Desktop App detects the crash and attempts to resume the interrupted conversation thread. However, the interrupted thread's rollout file is never written (crash happened before flush), so the App enters an infinite crash/resume loop: thread/resume succeeds but overrides are silently dropped, thread/archive fails with 'no rollout found', engine crashes again ~90s later. The only recovery is manual deletion of state_5.sqlite, session_index.jsonl, and sessions/.
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking: app becomes completely unusable in an infinite crash loop after any engine crash on Windows. Recovery requires manual database intervention, not just a restart. Strong log evidence with exact exit code, timestamped crash sequence, and multiple independent crash triggers. No workaround available.

source_issues.title: Any Single Engine Crash Leaves Orphaned Threads That Cause a Persistent Crash/Resume Loop
source_issues.evidence: Infinite crash/resume loop after any engine crash on Windows 11. Recovery requires manual deletion of state_5.sqlite*, session_index.jsonl, and sessions/. Root cause: crash before rollout flush leaves thread in interrupted state with no rollout file. Log evidence shows thread/resume overrides ignored, thread/archive fails with 'no rollout found', engine crashes with exit code 3221225786 every ~90 seconds.

signals.topic: MCP sub-agent processes never terminated on session stop/suspend — leads to OOM and system saturation
signals.summary: When a Codex CLI session is stopped (Ctrl+Z) or suspended on Linux, MCP server subprocesses are not terminated. Starting a new session on the same terminal layers new MCP processes on top of old ones. Over a work session this leads to massive process accumulation: 16 concurrent codex sessions, ~1500 total MCP-related child processes, 571 headless Chrome children from a single browser MCP, 8/8 GiB zram completely saturated on a 16 GiB machine. System became unusable due to accumulated processes alone. Cross-platform: macOS GUI (#16215) and Windows (#16144) also affected.
signals.review_reason: Direct path to OOM and system unavailability. Process audit data provides hard evidence: 16GB machine saturated by accumulated MCP processes. Cross-platform issue affecting Linux CLI, macOS GUI, and Windows. Repeatedly triggered by normal terminal job control (Ctrl+Z), a common workflow action. No teardown hook exists on session suspend.

source_issues.title: MCP sub-agent processes are never terminated when codex sessions are stopped/suspended
source_issues.evidence: Process audit on Linux: 16 concurrent codex sessions (most in stopped state), ~1500 total MCP-related child processes, 571 headless Chrome children from a single browser MCP, 8/8 GiB zram completely saturated on a 16 GiB machine. System became unusable due to accumulated processes alone. No SIGTSTP/SIGTERM cleanup hook fires when codex CLI session is suspended. Cross-platform: macOS GUI and Windows also affected.

signals.topic: SQLite databases grow unbounded on long-running installs — write lock contention causes app restart loop
signals.summary: On machines running Codex for months, state_5.sqlite and logs_1.sqlite grow to extreme sizes (~500MB+). PR #13781 reduced log retention from 90 to 10 days but is not retroactive — existing rows are never purged or VACUUMed. SQLite does not reclaim disk space after DELETE without VACUUM. At extreme sizes, write operations wait for read locks on bloated B-trees, creating contention that cascades into the app's cache layer, triggering repeated cache duplicate-write errors and an auto-restart loop that makes the app unusable.
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking through restart loop on long-running installs. Clear root cause (no VACUUM, non-retroactive retention policy) and measurable symptom (database sizes exceeding 500MB). Reproducible given enough usage time. No automatic mitigation exists, leading to progressive degradation and eventual app unavailability.

source_issues.title: state_5.sqlite and logs_1.sqlite grow unboundedly on long-running installs, causing write lock contention and app restart loop
source_issues.evidence: Explicit reproduction steps: run Codex Desktop for 3+ months, check database sizes at ~/.codex/*.sqlite*, observe auto-restart loop once combined size exceeds ~500MB. Root cause identified: PR #13781 retention reduction not retroactive, no VACUUM triggered. Log evidence of cache duplicate-write errors. No automatic mitigation — progressive degradation leading to complete app unavailability.

source_issues.title: my account has 'free tier' limits, when i'm on 'plus' plan.
