signals.topic: PowerShell launched with corrupted HOME path on Windows when username contains non-ASCII characters
signals.summary: On Windows with non-ASCII characters in the username (e.g., 'e'), Codex launches PowerShell with a corrupted HOME environment variable (e.g., 'C:\Users\rug\303\251' or mojibake). This causes PowerShell's built-in $HOME/~ to initialize incorrectly, breaks profile scripts, and prevents correct resolution of user directories. The issue occurs before PowerShell profile runs, meaning it cannot be patched from the profile. All tools relying on HOME or paths derived from it are broken inside the Codex terminal.
signals.review_reason: Terminal functionality broken for Windows users with international usernames. Clear reproduction path and root cause (encoding of user profile path before spawning pwsh). No user-side workaround for the $HOME initialization problem. Affects a large and growing user base with non-ASCII usernames globally.

source_issues.title: Windows: Codex launches PowerShell with corrupted HOME path when username contains 'e' (USERPROFILE/APPDATA can also be affected)
source_issues.evidence: Explicit reproduction steps for Windows with non-ASCII username. Verified: Windows registry shell folder values correct, HOME in HKCU\Environment correct, PowerShell works correctly in Windows Terminal. Codex logs show malformed path usage before shell profile executes. No user-side workaround for initial $HOME initialization problem.

signals.topic: hydrate_from_state stores id() of ephemeral objects in sent_items causing false-positive dedup after GC
signals.summary: When session is resumed via hydrate_from_state, the method stores id() of temporary dict objects in sent_items without keeping a strong reference. After garbage collection, CPython reuses the same memory address for later allocations, causing prepare_input to wrongly filter out legitimate new items as 'already sent', resulting in API 400 errors: 'No tool output found for function call'.
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed main-flow blocking bug in the conversation tracker that causes API-level failures after session resumption. The 400 error 'No tool output found for function call' is a complete workflow blocker for any agent using session persistence with human-in-the-loop approvals. Repro is deterministic and self-contained. The bug is acknowledged by maintainers (issue closed). No workaround exists — the false-positive dedup silently drops legitimate items from the API payload.

source_issues.title: hydrate_from_state stores id() of ephemeral objects in sent_items, causing false-positive dedup after GC
source_issues.evidence: Bug causes 400 API error 'No tool output found for function call <call_id>' after session resumption. Complete repro script provided. Hits HITL (human-in-the-loop) rejection workflow specifically. No workaround available — the bug is deterministic once session is resumed.

signals.topic: SDK rejects image_url type for base64 images when using Chat Completions API
signals.summary: When using set_default_openai_api('chat_completions') with Azure OpenAI, the SDK rejects content items with type='image_url' and only accepts 'input_image'. However, the Chat Completions API itself requires 'image_url' type. This creates an irreconcilable situation where neither type works correctly — SDK rejects image_url, but the API doesn't support input_image.
aliases: base64 image type rejection chat completions
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed workflow blocker for base64 image inputs when using Chat Completions API mode. Users cannot send images to Azure OpenAI via Chat Completions because the SDK only accepts 'input_image' type while the API requires 'image_url'. Neither option works end-to-end, making image processing completely unavailable in this API mode. Issue is acknowledged by maintainers (closed).

source_issues.title: Error when sending base64 image with type: image_url to Chat Completions API
source_issues.evidence: User reports SDK rejects 'image_url' type for Chat Completions API. When using 'input_image' (SDK-accepted type), Azure OpenAI completion API doesn't support it. This is a complete image-input workflow blocker for Chat Completions users.

signals.topic: Duplicate tool names across multiple MCP servers cause agent to hang indefinitely
signals.summary: When two or more MCP servers each contain a tool with the same internal tool name, running the agent causes the agent list to hang indefinitely and the agent becomes non-functional. The root cause is the SDK cannot distinguish between tools with identical names from different MCP servers. A documented workaround is to ensure all tool names are globally unique.
aliases: MCP duplicate tool names agent list freeze
signals.review_reason: This is a complete workflow blocker causing the agent to hang indefinitely when MCP tool name conflicts exist. Unlike intermittent issues, an infinite hang means the agent process is deadlocked with no recovery. The workaround (ensuring unique tool names) requires modifying MCP server configurations outside the SDK. The issue has been open since July 2025 without a fix, indicating a persistent gap in MCP tool name scoping. While count=1, the severity (infinite hang) and absence of an in-SDK fix justify P1.

source_issues.title: Duplicate tool names in multiple MCP tools cause the agent list to hang
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed bug causes agent list to hang indefinitely and renders agent non-functional. Root cause identified as tool name conflicts across MCP servers. Workaround exists (unique tool names) but requires user to manually fix MCP server configurations. Open issue with 1 comment, active as recently as 2026-03-26.

signals.topic: griffe vs griffelib version conflict causes ImportError crash in services and CI
signals.summary: When griffelib (v2.0.0) and griffe (v1.15.0) are both installed, they can overwrite each other depending on installation order, causing ImportError: 'cannot import name ExprInterpolation from griffe._internal.expressions'. This crashes the agent service and CI pipelines at import time.
signals.review_reason: This is a service/CI crash caused by a dependency version conflict between griffe and griffelib. While it causes import-time failures (blocking), the issue has a documented workaround (manually managing installation order via uv), and the fix (upgrading to griffelib 2+) requires no SDK code change — only a dependency version bump. Marked P2 because the workaround is accessible to users and the fix path is clear.

source_issues.title: maybe use griffelib instead of griffe as dependency, and update to 2+
source_issues.evidence: CI and service crash with ImportError at agents/tool.py import due to griffe/griffelib version conflict. Crash is deterministic when both packages are present with conflicting installation order. Workaround: manually manage package installation order.

signals.topic: ToolCallItem.to_input_item() drops title and description during session persistence round-trip
signals.summary: When persisting agent sessions via save_result_to_session, ToolCallItem's title and description fields are lost because to_input_item() calls model_dump(exclude_unset=True) on the raw item, which doesn't include SDK-local title/description fields. These fields survive in-memory but are dropped when writing to session storage, causing data loss on session resumption.
aliases: ToolCallItem title description lost on save
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed data-loss bug in session persistence. ToolCallItem's title and description fields are silently dropped during save_result_to_session because to_input_item() doesn't include SDK-local fields. Any agent relying on session persistence with named or described tool calls will lose this metadata on resumption. No workaround exists — users cannot preserve tool titles/descriptions across sessions.

source_issues.title: ToolCallItem.to_input_item() drops title and description on session persistence
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed data loss bug during session persistence. title and description fields set on ToolCallItem are silently dropped when to_input_item() is called in the save_result_to_session path. Self-contained Python repro shows both fields missing from output. Affects any agent using session persistence with named/described tool calls.

signals.topic: Responses API output_text property raises TypeError when model returns null text in content items
signals.summary: The Response.output_text property crashes with TypeError when the Responses API model returns an output_text content item with a null text field, instead of silently handling it. This is a main-flow-breaking error that prevents users from accessing response text.
signals.review_reason: Issue #3011 describes a clear runtime crash (TypeError from None concatenation) in a main API path — accessing response text. The bug is reproducible and blocks the primary use case of reading model output. Labeled 'bug' by maintainers. Count=1 (single issue), so P1 (not P0).

source_issues.title: Response.output_text fails to handle null text values in content items
source_issues.evidence: TypeError raised when accessing output_text property due to None concatenation when model returns text: null in output_text content items. Affects openai/gpt-oss-safeguard-120b model. Main flow is blocked — user cannot read response text.

signals.topic: Responses API undocumented reasoning+message pairing constraint causes silent 400 errors in multi-turn conversations
signals.summary: The Responses API requires reasoning and message items to appear as consecutive pairs in input, but this constraint is entirely undocumented. The common pattern of filtering response.output to keep only messages produces orphaned items that cause a 400 error on the next turn — silently breaking multi-turn conversations. Multiple SDKs and large projects (OpenClaw with 64.9k forks) are affected.
aliases: multi-turn conversation breakage due to undocumented API constraint
signals.review_reason: Issue #3009 describes a main-flow-breaking undocumented API constraint that silently corrupts multi-turn conversations — the most common developer pattern (filtering output to messages only) produces orphaned reasoning items causing guaranteed 400 on the next turn. Affects all 5 official OpenAI SDKs and a large production codebase (OpenClaw, 64.9k forks). This is a primary workflow blocker for any developer building multi-turn agents. Labeled 'bug'. Despite count=1, the severity and cross-SDK impact qualify as P0.

source_issues.title: Responses API: undocumented reasoning+message pairing constraint breaks multi-turn conversations
source_issues.evidence: Reproduced 400 error 'Item msg_... of type message was provided without its required preceding item of type reasoning' on gpt-5.3-codex and o4-mini. Affects all 5 official SDKs. OpenClaw (64.9k forks) had to add downgradeOpenAIReasoningBlocks() workaround. Undocumented constraint causes the most common pattern (filtering to msgs only) to silently produce broken state for the next turn.

signals.topic: jiter library corrupts tool call arguments by converting escaped double-quotes to escaped single-quotes
signals.summary: The jiter dependency corrupts the `arguments` string in tool call responses by converting escaped double-quotes (\") to escaped single-quotes (\'), producing invalid JSON that cannot be parsed by json.loads(). This breaks all tool/function calling with multi-field arguments for users of OpenAI-compatible servers (llama.cpp, vLLM, Ollama, etc.) using the OpenAI Python SDK.
signals.review_reason: Issue #2958 describes a data corruption bug in the SDK's jiter dependency that breaks tool/function calling — a key feature. The arguments JSON becomes unparseable, affecting both streamed and non-streamed responses. Real ecosystem impact confirmed (Home Assistant integrations). The bug is reproducible and the workaround requires users to manually patch the corrupted string, which is an unacceptable user burden for a core feature. Labeled 'bug'. Count=1, so P1.

source_issues.title: Tool call arguments field has escaped double-quotes converted to single-quotes by jiter
source_issues.evidence: Bug confirmed: raw HTTP response (verified via curl) contains correct JSON with \" escaping, but SDK deserialization corrupts to \'. json.loads() fails or produces wrong results. Affects both stream=True and stream=False. Impacts Home Assistant ecosystem (smart home integrations using llama.cpp/vLLM/Ollama). Workaround requires manual string replacement before parsing.

signals.topic: Windows spawn fails without shell:true — all terminal commands and agent commands return ENOENT on Node.js v22
signals.summary: On Windows, child_process.spawn() without shell:true cannot resolve commands from PATH or execute .cmd/.ps1 wrappers. This affects both terminal commands (git, node, cmd, etc.) via buildTerminalSpawnOptions() AND agent command spawning via the transport layer. On Node.js v22.12+, this returns EINVAL, making all ACP functionality completely unusable for Windows users.
signals.review_reason: Two issues with identical root cause (missing shell:true on Windows spawn) block ALL ACP functionality — both terminal commands and agent spawning. Issue #191 shows this is a Node.js v22.12+ regression affecting every Windows ACP user with zero working agent commands. Issue #169 shows every terminal command is broken. Combined count=2, open state, platform-wide impact on a core workflow makes this P0.

source_issues.title: Bug: spawn EINVAL on Windows with Node.js v22 — all agent commands fail
source_issues.evidence: All Windows users on Node.js v22 are affected; zero agent commands work (Codex, Claude, OpenCode, Gemini). EINVAL is a Node.js v22.12+ security change for .cmd/.ps1 wrappers without shell:true.

source_issues.title: Windows: terminal commands fail with ENOENT because buildTerminalSpawnOptions lacks shell:true
source_issues.evidence: Every terminal command (git, node, where, cmd) fails with spawn ENOENT on Windows. Root cause: buildTerminalSpawnOptions() does not set shell:true, preventing PATH resolution on Windows.

signals.topic: Persistent ACP sessions immediately reported dead ('queue owner unavailable') on macOS after creation
signals.summary: On macOS, acpx persistent sessions are created successfully but immediately report dead with 'queue owner unavailable' on status checks. This makes thread-bound persistent sessions completely unusable — the only workaround is ACP one-shot mode.
aliases: Persistent session queue owner unavailable macOS
Sessions dead immediately after ensure on macOS
signals.review_reason: Persistent sessions are a core acpx feature; their complete failure on macOS (a primary platform) with a clear repro steps and confirmed across multiple adapter versions represents a significant functional breakdown. count=1 precludes P0, but the 'queue owner unavailable' error with full workaround (disable persistent sessions) warrants P1.

source_issues.title: Persistent sessions become dead immediately (queue owner unavailable) on macOS
source_issues.evidence: Minimal repro shows sessions ensure succeeds but status immediately returns dead/queue owner unavailable. Reproduced across multiple acpx adapter versions (0.21.x, 0.23.1, 0.24.2). Thread-bound ACP sessions are completely unstable; workaround requires one-shot mode only.

signals.topic: ACP sessions permanently fail to start after gateway restart — error swallowing causes infinite dead session loop
signals.summary: After a gateway restart, ACP sessions fail to recover. createNamedSession silently swallows errors (returning null on any failure), ensureSession passes null upward, and recoverEnsureFailure incorrectly treats null as 'session already exists', counting it as resolved. This creates an infinite recovery loop with zero resolved sessions.
aliases: Gateway restart causes permanent session failure
signals.review_reason: Gateway restart is a standard operational action that should be resilient. The three-layer error swallowing anti-pattern (null as universal error sentinel) causes a permanent failure loop with zero recovery. This is a core reliability failure for a persistent session system. count=1 precludes P0, but the severity (permanent unrecoverable state after a routine operation) warrants P1.

source_issues.title: ACP session spawn fails silently after gateway restart — error swallowing leads to dead session loop
source_issues.evidence: acp startup identity reconcile reports resolved=0 failed=N — all sessions fail after restart, none recover. Three-layer error swallowing (createNamedSession → ensureSession → recoverEnsureFailure) creates an infinite recovery loop. Exit code 3 (TIMEOUT) from dead queue owner is misinterpreted at every layer.

signals.topic: ACP protocolVersion type mismatch — acpx sends string '1.0', Gemini CLI expects number 1
signals.summary: acpx sends protocolVersion as a string ('1.0') in the initialize handshake, but Gemini CLI strictly requires a number (1). This blocks the entire ACP handshake with Gemini CLI, making Gemini integration impossible.
aliases: Gemini CLI ACP protocolVersion type mismatch
ACP initialize handshake fails with Gemini
signals.review_reason: Protocol type mismatch is a clear interop bug that blocks Gemini ACP integration entirely. However, count=1 and single-agent impact (Gemini only, while Codex and Claude work) makes this P2 rather than P1. The fix is straightforward (cast protocolVersion to number), but until fixed, Gemini ACP is completely unusable.

source_issues.title: ACP: protocolVersion type mismatch with Gemini CLI (--acp)
source_issues.evidence: Gemini CLI returns -32603 with message 'expected number, received string' for protocolVersion field. Full handshake fails, preventing any Gemini ACP integration. Codex and Claude work fine; Gemini is the sole affected agent.

signals.topic: Agent config 'args' field silently ignored in parseAgents() — custom agents requiring arguments fail silently
signals.summary: The parseAgents() function in config.ts reads the 'command' field but completely ignores the 'args' array from ~/.acpx/config.json. This causes agent processes (e.g., Cursor CLI with 'agent acp' subcommand) to spawn without intended arguments, leading to ACP protocol initialization hangs. No error is thrown, making diagnosis difficult.
aliases: Custom agent arguments not passed through
signals.review_reason: Silent failure in agent configuration parsing blocks any agent requiring arguments (e.g., Cursor CLI 'agent acp' pattern). The absence of error feedback makes this particularly insidious — users see ACP initialization hang with no diagnostic. count=1 and limited scope (agents with args) makes this P2, but the silent/hard-to-diagnose nature is notable.

source_issues.title: fix: parseAgents() ignores 'args' field in ~/.acpx/config.json agents config
source_issues.evidence: Config schema documents args as supported, parseAgents() silently discards it. Agent process starts but without correct subcommand, causing ACP protocol initialization to hang indefinitely. Users cannot configure agents requiring arguments.

signals.topic: Gateway enters infinite model-switch loop when all auth profiles fail — gateway completely unresponsive

signals.topic: max_tokens config leaks across providers causing HTTP 403 in multi-provider eval
signals.summary: In multi-provider evaluations, setting max_tokens on one provider (e.g., gpt-4.1-mini) causes that parameter to leak to other providers (e.g., gpt-5.4-mini) that don't define it. Since gpt-5.4-mini rejects max_tokens and requires max_completion_tokens, the leaked parameter causes HTTP 403 failures, blocking the entire eval for affected providers.
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow blocking bug: multi-provider evals fail entirely (HTTP 403) when mixing model families that accept max_tokens vs. those that require max_completion_tokens. The root cause is config isolation failure across providers, directly causing eval pipeline to break. Reproducer provided with specific model families (gpt-4.1-mini vs. gpt-5.4-mini). Count=1 but P0 due to the severe blocking nature (eval cannot complete for the second provider) and clear user impact.

This is a config isolation bug where provider configs are not fully isolated.

signals.topic: Google Reranker post-processor fails in production deployments due to async threading issue
signals.summary: The async `_apostprocess_nodes` method in the Google Reranker post-processor uses `RankServiceAsyncClient` which causes thread-related failures in production environments (e.g., deployed React agents). The virtual assistant returns 'technical issues with tools' errors. The sync fallback path (`asyncio.to_thread`) works fine, indicating the async client is the root cause. Affects production RAG pipelines where Google reranking is needed.

signals.review_reason: Production RAG pipeline failure — the Google reranker works in development but breaks in production environments, causing the agent to fail and return error messages to end users. High comment count (7) suggests community-wide impact. This is a main-flow blocking issue for production deployments using Google reranking.

Using `asyncio.to_thread` workaround makes it work. 7 comments indicate community interest and likely others affected.

signals.topic: to_openai_responses_message_dict serializes input_file with incorrect nested 'file' object, breaking OpenAI Responses API calls
signals.summary: The `to_openai_responses_message_dict` function nests file data under a 'file' key (`{type: 'input_file', file: {filename, file_data}}`) when serializing DocumentBlocks. This does not match the current OpenAI Responses API schema which expects flat `input_file` objects with `filename` and `file_data` directly on the top-level item. Results in API rejection/failure when uploading files via the Responses API.
aliases: OpenAI Responses API input_file schema mismatch
DocumentBlock serialization wrong schema for Responses API
signals.review_reason: API-level breaking issue — the serialized payload does not conform to OpenAI's documented Responses API schema, causing file attachment operations via the Responses API path to fail. Affects any user trying to use file upload features with the newer Responses API. Non-trivial comment count (4) confirms community impact.

signals.topic: Multiple bugs in OpenAI LLM integration causing data loss and incorrect behavior in multi-turn tool-calling workflows
signals.summary: Six compounding bugs in the OpenAI LLM integration: (1) Assistant text silently dropped when tool calls present in same message; (2) Response phase not preserved on parsing; (3) Phase not serialized back to API; (4) Reasoning/sampling params gated on exact model name lookup, missing dated snapshots; (5) Reasoning token count duplicated across all ThinkingBlocks; (6) Tool call arguments not consistently JSON-serialized. These break GPT-5.4 multi-turn tool workflows where the model emits commentary + tool calls tagged with phase.
aliases: OpenAI Responses API multi-turn workflow data loss
GPT-5.4 multi-turn tool call assistant text dropped
OpenAI reasoning model params silently dropped for dated snapshots
tool call arguments not JSON serialized in Responses API
signals.review_reason: Data loss + workflow degradation in GPT-5.4 multi-turn tool-calling — assistant text (model's reasoning/preamble) is silently dropped when tool calls are present, breaking conversation history fidelity. Additionally, reasoning params are silently dropped for newly released dated model snapshots. These are not minor bugs; they degrade LLM output quality and break standard workflows. Six compounding bugs from a single detailed report covering the critical OpenAI integration path.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Multiple bugs in llama-index-llms-openai
source_issues.evidence: Bug #1: assistant pre-tool-call text is silently dropped when serializing messages with tool calls, losing model reasoning commentary critical for GPT-5.4. Bug #2-3: 'phase' metadata (commentary vs final_answer) is lost on round-trip. Bug #4: reasoning params silently dropped for valid dated model snapshots (e.g., gpt-5.4-2026-03-05) not pre-listed in O1_MODELS dict. Bug #6: tool call arguments not JSON-serialized, causing API errors. These are not edge cases — they affect standard GPT-5.4 tool-calling workflows. Detailed sub-bugs table provided.

signals.topic: Refine synthesizer crashes with uncaught ValueError/TypeError when tool-calling structured outputs fail
signals.summary: When using `output_cls` with a function-calling LLM in the Refine synthesizer, if the LLM fails to produce valid tool calls (raising ValueError) or returns a non-BaseModel tool output (raising TypeError), these exceptions are uncaught. The Refine synthesizer only catches ValidationError, so the query fails with an unhandled traceback instead of falling back to a warning/graceful degradation path. This was introduced after v0.14.18.
aliases: Refine synthesizer uncaught exception on structured output failure
structured_predict ValueError crashes Refine query engine
tool-calling structured output error not caught in Refine
signals.review_reason: Main query flow crash — when structured output tool-calling fails (common scenario with misconfigured LLMs or API issues), the Refine synthesizer crashes instead of gracefully degrading. This blocks the entire query, whereas the codebase has an existing graceful degradation path for ValidationError that should also apply here. 3 comments confirm community hit.

source_issues.evidence: Reproducer provided: with a fake API key, patching FunctionCallingProgram to raise ValueError causes the Refine synthesizer to crash with an unhandled traceback. signals.topic: QueryFusionRetriever blocks async event loop during synchronous LLM query generation, freezing concurrent coroutines
signals.summary: QueryFusionRetriever._aretrieve() calls synchronous _get_queries() which blocks on LLM.complete() instead of awaiting an async equivalent. When num_queries > 1 (the default), this blocks the current event loop during query expansion, preventing other coroutines on the same loop from making progress. Other async tasks are frozen for the full duration of the synchronous HTTP call.
aliases: asyncio event loop freeze in QueryFusionRetriever
signals.review_reason: Async correctness bug — the synchronous LLM call inside an async method blocks the event loop, freezing all other coroutines for the duration of an HTTP call. This breaks concurrent async applications. While only 1 issue report, the bug is a fundamental async anti-pattern that would affect any async application using QueryFusionRetriever (num_queries defaults to >1). The reproducer clearly demonstrates the freeze.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: `QueryFusionRetriever._aretrieve` blocks the event loop during query generation
source_issues.evidence: Reproducer provided: asyncio task scheduled alongside retriever.aretrieve() is frozen for the full duration of the LLM HTTP call, even though it only needs 0.1s. Task.done() returns False after expected 0.1s. This is a fundamental async correctness bug affecting any async application using QueryFusionRetriever with num_queries > 1 (the default).

signals.topic: streamText parsePartialOutput creates O(n) string copies causing 350MB+ memory per stream and OOM kills in production
signals.summary: streamText with default text() output calls JSON.stringify on accumulated text for every streaming chunk. For a 110KB response in 13,000 chunks this creates ~350MB of retained string objects per stream, leading to OOM kills on containers with 3+ concurrent streams.
signals.review_reason: Production crash caused by memory exhaustion: 3.4GB heap usage from 3 concurrent streams leading to OOM kills. Heap snapshot evidence shows 14,351 string copies (1.6GB) from JSON.stringify inside streaming loop. V8 large_object_space at 55% of total heap. This is a high-severity memory regression affecting any production deployment handling concurrent long-output streams.

source_issues.title: streamText Memory Issue: parsePartialOutput creates O(n) string copies
source_issues.evidence: Heap snapshot shows 14,351 string copies totaling 1.6GB from single stream. With 3 concurrent streams heap reached 3.4GB causing OOM on 4GB container. 55% of total heap in large_object_space at peak. Root cause: JSON.stringify forces V8 ConsString flattening on every chunk.

signals.topic: @ai-sdk/google: cannot combine provider-defined tools (googleSearch) with custom function tools — Gemini 3 tool combination broken

Has clear reproduction case and verified fix.

signals.topic: @ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock: doStream() and doGenerate() do not return request body — breaking observability and tracing
signals.summary: BedrockChatLanguageModel.doStream() and doGenerate() do not return a 'request' field in their return objects. Observability frameworks like Mastra rely on this field to populate tracing span inputs; with Bedrock it is always undefined, resulting in empty span attributes.
signals.review_reason: Observability gap: Bedrock provider omits the 'request' field that all other providers return, breaking tracing and span input population in observability frameworks like Mastra. Users cannot see what context/messages were sent to the LLM when using Bedrock. The TODO comment in source confirms this is a known unimplemented gap, not a design limitation.

source_issues.title: @ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock: doStream() and doGenerate() do not return request body

signals.topic: @ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock: negative noCacheTokens and incorrect total tokens computed for prompt-cached requests
signals.summary: Bedrock usage conversion computes noCache as inputTokens - cacheReadTokens, but Bedrock's inputTokens already excludes cached tokens. This produces negative values (e.g., 1 - 6512 = -6511) and wrong totals, breaking usage reporting and cost tracking.
signals.review_reason: Usage reporting broken for Bedrock prompt caching: negative noCacheTokens (-6511) and wrong total (1 vs 7304) break cost tracking, billing reconciliation, and observability. Clear root cause identified in source code with direct comparison to correct Anthropic provider implementation. Issue is closed (presumably fixed) confirming it's a real bug.

source_issues.title: Bug: @ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock computes negative noCacheTokens for cached requests
source_issues.evidence: Example Bedrock response: inputTokens=1, cacheReadInputTokens=6512, cacheWriteInputTokens=791. SDK computes noCache: 1-6512=-6511 (should be 1) and total: 1 (should be 7304). Anthropic provider uses direct assignment correctly. Bug affects any usage reporting or cost tracking.
